provisions of this Charter.
Any secretary appointed by the Mayor under the provisions of this Section who
is covered by the classified civil service provisions of this Charter shall
retain all of the rights and benefits thereof. All other secretaries appointed
by the Mayor under this Section shall be exempted from said provisions.
Sec. 5.09. - Chief Administrative Officer.
For the purpose of providing professional assistance and continuity in the
administration of the Merged Government, the Council shall select and employ a
Chief Administrative Officer. No person shall be selected or employed as the
Chief Administrative Officer unless he or she shall possess demonstrable
educational and/or professional experience in the art and science of
governmental management as required of such office. Said officer may be a non-
resident of Kentucky and/or the Urban County, but must become a resident of the
area served by the Merged Government within six (6) months and shall maintain
such residence during the tenure of his or her office. The Chief Administrative
Officer shall be compensated at a rate determined by the Council.
The Chief Administrative Officer may be removed without cause by a three-fifths
( 3/5 ) vote of the entire Council during his first year of service. After one
(1) year of service, the Chief Administrative Officer may be removed without
cause by a three-fifths ( 3/5 ) vote of the entire Council, provided that he
shall be granted six (6) months notice of the council's intention to remove
him, or in the alternative he shall be granted six (6) months severance pay.
After one (1) year of service a Chief Administrative Officer may be removed at
any time for sufficient cause or willful neglect of duty by a three-fifths ( 3/
5 ) vote of the Council, provided that the Council supply the Chief
Administrative Officer a written statement of the charges against him and
afford him an opportunity to appear before a public hearing held by the Council
within thirty (30) days of notifying him of the charges. The Chief
Administrative Officer may be represented by counsel and present evidence at
said hearing and may appeal to the courts any decision of the Council to remove
him for cause or willful neglect of duty. In no case shall the Council effect
the removal of a Chief Administrative Officer by a reduction in his
compensation.
Whenever a vacancy shall exist in the office of Chief Administrative Officer, a
committee composed of the Mayor and four (4) Council members appointed by the
Vice-Mayor shall solicit and evaluate applicants for said position, and shall
recommend to the Council one or more candidates for the position. The Council
shall then select and employ a Chief Administrative Officer by a vote of a
majority of its entire membership.
Annotation—KRS 67A.025 provides for the hiring, termination and severance pay
of the Chief Administrative Officer.
Sec. 5.10. - Powers and Duties of the Chief Administrative Officer.
The Chief Administrative Officer shall:
A.   Exercise direct administrative control and supervision over the Office of
Administrative Services as provided for in
Article Six of this Charter.
B.   Recommend to the Mayor, in pursuance of the provisions of Section
5.04 of this Charter, persons to be appointed as Department Commissioners.
C.   Subject to the authority of the Mayor as stated in this Charter, supervise
and control all departments created by
Article Six of this Charter or by ordinance pursuant thereto; the Commissioners
of which shall report directly to the Chief Administrative Officer.
D.   Serve as the liaison officer between the Mayor and such other agencies,
boards, commissions and authorities as the Mayor may designate.
E.   Recommend to the Mayor the annual operating and capital improvements
budgets.
F.   Make periodic reports, with such recommendations as he deems appropriate,
to the Mayor and the Council concerning the operation, affairs and future needs
of the Merged Government.
G.   Examine regularly, at periods fixed by the Mayor and/or the Council, the
accounts, records and operations of every department, agency, board, commission
or authority receiving financial appropriations from the Merged Government.
H.   Perform such other duties not inconsistent with the provisions of this
Charter as the Mayor or the Council may prescribe.
ARTICLE 6. - EXECUTIVE DEPARTMENTS AND THE OFFICE OF ADMINISTRATIVE SERVICES 3
 
Notes
  Annotation—Many of these departments and divisions have been reorganized or
3 renamed pursuant to Section
  6.12.
Sec. 6.01. - General Provisions.
The Merged Government Council shall create and otherwise provide for an Office
of Administrative Services. In addition, the Council shall create and otherwise
provide for the following Executive Departments:
1.   Department of Law
2.   Department of Finance
3.   Department of Public Safety
4.   Department of Parks and Recreation
5.   Department of Social Services
6.   Department of Sanitation and Public Works
7.   Department of Housing and Community Development
The Office of Administrative Services and each of the aforementioned Executive
Departments shall be organized into such divisions as may be provided in this
Charter or by ordinance passed by the Council pursuant thereto. All matters
pertaining to the internal organization of the Office of Administrative
Services and the Executive Departments below the division level shall be left
to the discretion of the Council.
Sec. 6.02. - Principal Officers of the Executive Branch.
The Office of Administrative Services shall be under the direct control of the
Chief Administrative Officer as provided in Section
5.10 of this Charter.
The Commissioner of each department shall be appointed by the Mayor, subject to
the provisions of Sections
5.04 and
5.10 of this Charter.
All Department Commissioners shall be appointed on the basis of their
respective executive, administrative and professional qualifications, and shall
receive such compensation as may be prescribed by ordinance of the Council. Any
persons appointed as a Department Commissioner shall serve at the pleasure of
the Mayor, and the position of Department Commissioner shall be exempted from
the civil service provisions of this Charter or any ordinance passed by the
Council pursuant thereto.
Except as otherwise provided in Section
15.08 of this Charter, no person shall be appointed as an acting, interim or
temporary Department Commissioner unless said appointment is to fill a vacancy
created by death, removal, resignation or retirement; nor shall any person be
appointed to the position of acting, interim or temporary Department
Commissioner for a period of more than six (6) consecutive months. Any person
appointed as an acting, interim or temporary Department Commissioner who is
covered by the classified civil service and/or employee pension provisions of
this Charter on the date of such appointment, shall retain all of the rights
and privileges thereof. However, any acting, interim or temporary Department
Commissioner covered by said provisions who wishes to accept a regular
appointment as a Department Commissioner shall be removed from the classified
civil service in accordance with the provisions of Section
9.02 of this Charter. All matters pertaining to the pension rights of said
persons shall be resolved in accordance with the provisions of Section
9.08 of this Charter.
Sec. 6.03. - Division Directors and Employees.
Each division within the Office of Administrative Services and the various
Executive Departments shall be headed by a Division Director. Except as
otherwise provided, all Division Directors shall be under the classified civil
service system of the Merged Government.
All employees of a division below the rank of Division Director shall be under
the classified civil service system of the Merged Government unless
specifically prohibited by law or exempted under the provisions of this
Charter.
Sec. 6.04. - Office of Administrative Services.
The Office of Administrative Services shall be organized into a Division of
Personnel, a Division of Budgeting, a Division of Federal Programs, and such
other divisions as the Council may prescribe.
The Division of Personnel shall be responsible for the administration of all
personnel programs of the Merged Government, including such civil service
programs as may be established under the provisions of this Charter. Said
division shall also assist all pension fund boards created or established under
the provisions of this Charter in the administration of all employee pension
programs. It shall be the particular duty of the Division of Personnel to keep
all employees informed of their pension rights, process all applications for
pension claims, and perform such other administrative duties as the various
pension fund boards of the Merged Government may direct.
The Division of Budgeting shall be charged with assisting the Chief
Administrative Officer and the Mayor with the preparation of the annual
operating and capital improvements budgets. It shall provide for the periodic
review of said budgets and conduct such budgeting studies and long range
forecasts as the Chief Administrative Officer may direct. It shall prepare and
administer, under the supervision of the Chief Administrative Officer, a system
of program budgeting for the Merged Government, and shall prepare and
administer all official forms for gathering budgetary data and requests from
all departments, agencies, boards and commissions receiving funds from the
Merged Government.
The Division of Federal Programs shall be responsible for the coordination of
all federal grant applications of the Merged Government. It shall assist any
department, division, agency, board or commission of the Merged Government with
the preparation of all federal grant applications and shall keep all
departments, divisions, agencies, boards and commissions informed of all
federal programs relevant to them.
Sec. 6.05. - Department of Law.
The Department of Law shall be organized into a Division of Litigation, a
Division of Corporate Counsel, and such other divisions as the Council may
prescribe. The Department Commissioner and all Division Directors of said
department shall be qualified attorneys-at-law.
The Division of Litigation shall be charged with the performance of all duties
associated with the preparation and conduct of all legal proceedings in which
the Merged Government, its departments, divisions, agencies, boards and
commissions, may be a party.
The Division of Corporate Counsel shall be charged with the preparation of all
contracts and other legal instruments of the Merged Government; and shall
provide such legal advice and assistance as the Merged Government, its Council,
executive departments, boards and commissions may require.
No division in the Department of Law shall engage in any activity which would
infringe upon the powers and duties of the County Attorney as the prosecuting
attorney for the Lexington-Fayette Urban County Government. Nor shall any
division in said department engage in any activity related to the powers and
duties of the County Attorney as a legal officer under law for various state
agencies.
Sec. 6.06. - Department of Finance.
The Department of Finance shall be organized into a Division of the Treasury, a
Division of Accounting, a Division of Data Processing, a Division of Tax
Collection, a Division of Central Purchasing, and such other divisions as the
Council may prescribe.
The Division of the Treasury shall be responsible for the custody, investment
and disbursement of all funds of the Merged Government in accordance with the
procedures and standards established by the Council.
The Division of Accounting shall be responsible for the maintenance of a
general accounting system for the Merged Government, including auditing and
cost control records and procedures, pre-auditing procedures for all claims on
the funds of the Merged Government, and a current audit of all cash receipts
received and due the Merged Government.
The Division of Data Processing shall provide all computer and other data
processing services required by the Department of Finance and such other
departments, agencies, boards and commissions as may be authorized or required
to use such services.
The Division of Tax Collection shall be charged with the collection of all
income, revenues and moneys due the Merged Government. The County Sheriff,
elected under the Constitution and laws of Kentucky shall continue to collect
all taxes levied by the Merged Government which are to be collected under law
by County Sheriffs. All taxes collected by the Sheriff shall be filed with the
Director of the Division of Tax Collection. The Director of the Division of Tax
Collection shall be responsible for collecting all taxes levied by the Merged
Government not covered by the law pertaining to the tax collection duties of
the County Sheriff. All receipts of said division shall be forwarded, under
procedures established by the Council, to the Division of the Treasury for
custody and deposit.
The Division of Central Purchasing shall be responsible for making all
purchases for the Merged Government, its departments, agencies, divisions and
such boards and commissions as the Council may direct. Said division shall
administer a system of centralized purchasing best suited to obtain the
greatest economic savings and value in the procurement of all necessary
supplies, materials, equipment, contractual services, insurance and surety
bonds, and such other items as may be prescribed by the Council.
Annotation—The duties of the division of tax collection may be satisfied by a
contract with an outside agency. Jacobs v. LFUCG, supra, at 14. The tax
collection duties of the sheriff have been contracted to the Urban County
Government pursuant to an annual purchase of service agreement.
Sec. 6.07. - Department of Public Safety.
The Department of Public Safety shall be organized into a Division of Police, a
Division of Building Inspection, a Division of Fire Protection, a Division of
Detention, a Division of Animal Control, a Division of Civil Defense, and such
other divisions as the Council may prescribe.
The Division of Police shall be responsible for general law enforcement in the
Urban County and shall be organized and equipped to provide general police
services throughout the General Services District and such additional police
services as may be deemed necessary for the protection of lives and property in
the Full Urban Services District. The Director of said division shall hold the
rank of Chief of Police and shall be professionally trained and experienced in
the art and sciences of police work.
The Division of Fire Protection shall be responsible for the provision of fire
prevention and protection services in the Urban County, and shall be organized
and equipped to provide general fire protection services throughout the General
Services District and such additional fire services as may be deemed necessary
for the protection of lives and property in the Full Urban Services District.
The Director of said division shall hold the rank of Fire Chief and shall be
professionally trained and experienced in the operation and management of fire
prevention and protection services.
The Division of Detention shall be responsible for the detention and security
of all prisoners assigned to the custody of the Merged Government under law,
excepting those assigned to the care and custody of the Division of Juvenile
Detention and Probation pursuant to Section
6.09 of this Charter. The Division of Detention shall be responsible for the
operation of the County Jail and the City of Lexington Jail (workhouse). The
latter shall be designated as a county workhouse under the provisions of KRS
441.070 thru 441.205. The County Jailer, elected under the provisions of
Section
11.07 of this Charter, shall be designated as the Director of the Division of
Detention.
The Division of Building Inspection shall perform all of the duties and
functions pertaining to the inspection and safety of buildings and other
structures performed by the Department of Building Inspection of the City of
Lexington on the effective date of this Charter. Said division shall administer
and enforce all zoning ordinances.
The Division of Animal Control shall enforce all laws and ordinances pertaining
to the licensing, inspection and control of animals in the General Services
District, which shall be the same as those imposed by order of the Fayette
County Fiscal Court on the effective date of this Charter, and the Full Urban
Services District, which shall be the same as those imposed by the City of
Lexington on the effective date of this Charter. The Director of said division
shall be designated as the county dog warden under the provisions of KRS
258.195, and shall coordinate the activities of the Division of Animal Control
with the county livestock inspector to be appointed by the Council in
accordance with the provisions of KRS 257.280.
The Division of Civil Defense shall be charged with the operation and
administration of a civil defense program for a Merged Government in accordance
with the state civil defense plan and program. The Director of said division
shall be appointed by the Mayor in accordance with the provisions of KRS 39.415
until such time as the General Assembly may provide for the Director of Civil
Defense in an urban county government to be covered by civil service.
Annotation—(1) Additional fire and police protection have been deleted as
additional urban services. See note at Section
2.08.
   (2) Ordinance No. 52-76 deleted and abolished the division of detention from
the department of public safety. Subsequently, the office of jailer was
abolished effective January 3, 1994, by 1990 Ky. Acts Ch. 138, and pursuant to
that Act the division of detention was recreated by Ordinance No. 238-93.
   (3) Resolution No. 250-75 and Ordinance No. 25-76 had the effect of deleting
the division of animal control from the department of public safety and placed
that service with the Lexington Humane Society. Too, the Lexington Humane
Society was appointed Fayette County Dog Warden pursuant to Resolution No. 286-
91. Further, KRS 257.280, relating to the county livestock inspector, was
repealed by 1978 Ky. Acts Ch. 118, § 19, effective June 17, 1978.
   (4) KRS 39.415, relating to civil defense, was repealed by 1998 Ky. Acts Ch.
226, § 113, effective July 15, 1998.
Sec. 6.08. - Department of Parks and Recreation.
The Department of Parks and Recreation shall be organized into a Division of
Parks, a Division of Recreation, and such other divisions as the Council may
prescribe.
The Division of Parks shall equip, maintain and operate all parks, playgrounds,
swimming pools and golf courses of the Merged Government.
The Division of Recreation shall be responsible for planning, organizing,
staffing, equipping and operating all recreational and leisure time programs
and activities provided by the Merged Government.
Sec. 6.09. - Department of Social Services.
The Department of Social Services shall be organized into a Division of
Welfare, a Division of Homes, a Division of Juvenile Detention and Probation, a
Division of Children's Services, and such other divisions as the Council of the
Merged Government may prescribe.
The Division of Welfare shall be responsible for all welfare and social service
programs administered by the welfare departments of the City of Lexington and
the County of Fayette on the effective date of this Charter, and such other
welfare and social service programs as may be established under law by the
Council of the Merged Government. In addition, said division shall be
responsible for the administration of all duties assigned to the Domestic
Relations Office of the County of Fayette on the effective date of this
Charter.
The Division of Homes shall be responsible for the operation and administration
of the Julius Marks Home of Fayette County as the same existed on the effective
date of this Charter, and such other homes and refuge places as the Council of
the Merged Government may designate. The Director of said division shall be the
director of the Julius Marks Home.
The Division of Juvenile Detention and Probation shall administer all juvenile
detention and probation programs under law as provided by the Kincaid Home and
the Juvenile Probation Office operating under the Fayette County Juvenile Court
on the effective date of this Charter, and such other juvenile programs as the
Merged Government Council may prescribe. Said division shall serve as the
administrative agency for enforcing all juvenile detention and probation orders
of the Juvenile Division of the County Court as specified in
Article Ten of this Charter.
The Division of Children's Services shall perform all of the duties and
functions of the Fayette County Children's Bureau as they are defined under law
on the effective date of this Charter.
Sec. 6.10. - Department of Sanitation and Public Works.
The Department of Sanitation and Public Works shall be organized into a
Division of Refuse Collection and Disposal, a Division of Sanitary Sewers, a
Division of Streets and Roads, a Division of Property Maintenance, a Division
of Engineering, a Division of Traffic Engineering, and such other divisions as
the Merged Government Council may designate.
The Division of Refuse Collection and Disposal shall be responsible for the
collection and proper disposal of all trash and garbage collected by the Merged
Government and shall regulate the disposal of all garbage and trash collected
by private persons.
The Division of Sanitary Sewers shall operate and maintain the sanitary sewer
system of the Merged Government. Initially this system shall be the same as
that owned and operated by the City of Lexington on the effective date of this
Charter, including all sewage disposal plants of the City of Lexington.
The Division of Streets and Roads shall construct, service and maintain all
streets and roads of the Merged Government, including those streets and roads
serviced and maintained by the City of Lexington and the County of Fayette on
the effective date of this Charter.
The Division of Property Maintenance shall service and maintain all buildings
and other structures owned by the Merged Government not specifically covered by
other sections of this Charter.
The Division of Engineering shall perform all engineering duties for the Merged
Government, including those functions performed by the City Engineer for the
City of Lexington on the effective date of this Charter.
The Division of Traffic Engineering shall perform all traffic engineering
services for the Merged Government, including those performed by the City
Traffic Engineer of the City of Lexington on the effective date of this
Charter.
Sec. 6.11. - Department of Housing and Community Development.
The Department of Housing and Community Development shall be organized into a
Division of Housing Services, a Division of Urban Renewal, a Division of
Planning, and such other divisions as the Merged Government Council may
designate.
The Division of Housing Services shall identify housing problems and
deficiencies within the territory of the Merged Government. Except as otherwise
provided in Section
7.12 of this Charter, said division shall be responsible for planning,
coordinating and administering all activities of the Merged Government related
to the work of various public and private agencies concerned with housing
problems.
The Division of Urban Renewal shall be responsible for the administration and
operation of all urban renewal programs of the Merged Government, including
such urban renewal programs as may be funded or otherwise implemented by the
City of Lexington or the County of Fayette on the effective date of this
Charter.
The Division of Planning shall be responsible for preparing, updating and
continuous revision of all community development plans and proposals. Said
division shall provide such professional planning and staff services to the
Planning Commission and the Board of Zoning Appeals as may have been provided
by the entire professional staff of the Lexington-Fayette County Planning
Commission on the effective date of this Charter.
Sec. 6.12. - General Powers of the Council Over Departments, Divisions and
Offices.
The Council of the Merged Government shall have the power to consolidate,
divide, and otherwise restructure the organization of all departments, offices
and divisions covered by this Article, provided that:
(a)   Any ordinance to consolidate, divide or otherwise restructure said
departments, offices and divisions shall be passed by a three-fifths ( 3/5 )
vote of the Council; and
(b)   The substance of such action by the Council is consistent with the
Constitution and laws of the Commonwealth of Kentucky governing the
administration of the functions or services involved by counties and/or cities
of the second class.
ARTICLE 7. - BOARDS, COMMISSIONS AND AUTHORITIES
Sec. 7.01. - General Provisions.
On the effective date of this Charter the following boards and commissions
shall be terminated:
(a)   The Police and Fire Merit Board of Fayette County;
(b)   The Parks and Recreation Board of Fayette County;
(c)   The Board of Equalization of the City of Lexington;
(d)   The Executive Board of the Fayette County Children's Bureau; and
(e)   The Lexington Urban Renewal and Community Development Agency.
All city, county or joint city-county boards, agencies and commissions as may
exist on the effective date of this Charter which are not specifically provided
for in this Charter shall continue for a period of ninety (90) days during
which time the Council shall determine, by ordinance, whether they shall be
continued or terminated. In the event the Council fails to act within the
specified time limit, said boards, agencies and commissions, advisory or
otherwise, shall cease to exist.
The Council shall have the power to create by ordinance such boards, agencies
and commissions as may be provided under law for cities of the second class
and/or counties containing cities of the second class, provided that such
ordinance is consistent with the terms of this Charter.
Annotation—Sections 7.01(e) and
7.13—The provisions for the termination of the Lexington Urban Renewal and
Community Development Agency and the transfer of its functions to the division
of urban renewal were held invalid. Holsclaw v. Stephens, supra, at 479-480.
See Ordinances No. 31-74 and 114-74, which continued boards, agencies and
commissions not specifically provided for in the Charter.
Sec. 7.02. - Terms, Compensation and Qualifications of Members.
Except as otherwise provided by this Charter or appropriate state law, all
members of boards, agencies and commissions covered by the provisions of this
Article shall be appointed by the Mayor subject to confirmation by a majority
of the council members.
Except as otherwise provided by law, the terms of board, agency and commission
members shall be four (4) years, provided that said terms shall be staggered in
such manner as to allow the appointment or re-appointment of at least one-half
of the membership of any board, agency or commission every two (2) years.
All vacancies on any board, agency or commission shall be filled for the
unexpired term in the manner prescribed for original appointment by this
Charter or by applicable state law. Any member of a board, agency or commission
may be removed from office in accordance with applicable state law, or in the
absence of such law, by a majority of the Council of the Merged Government.
Except as otherwise provided by applicable state law, the Council may prescribe
by ordinance for the compensation and/or reimbursement of actual and necessary
expenses incurred by members of any board or commission created by this Charter
or by ordinance passed pursuant thereto.
The Council may, subject to the limitations of applicable state law, prescribe
the qualifications required of any member of the boards, agencies and
commissions covered by the provisions of this Charter. In addition, the Council
may, within the limits set by this Charter or applicable state law, provide any
board, agency or commission with such clerical, secretarial or other staff
assistance as may be deemed necessary.
All official meetings of boards, agencies and commissions of the Merged
Government shall be public and any citizen shall have access to the minutes and
official records thereof on request.
Annotation—With respect to mayoral appointments to boards and commissions, see
also Section
5.04. Further, the provisions of this section relating to open meetings and
records have in some instances been superseded by KRS 61.805 et seq., and KRS
61.870 et seq.
Sec. 7.03. - Civil Service Commission.
On the effective date of this Charter, the Lexington Civil Service Commission
and the Lexington Civil Service Examining Board shall together constitute the
"Civil Service Commission" of the Merged Government. Said commission shall
advise and assist the Director of Personnel in the Office of Administrative
Services and the Chief Administrative Officer on matters pertaining to the
operation and administration of the classified civil service system of the
Merged Government within the terms and limitations set forth in
Article Nine of this Charter. All vacancies on said commission shall be filled
by the Mayor subject to confirmation by a majority of the council members.
Within one (1) year of the effective date of this Charter, said board and
commission shall be consolidated into a single, five-member Civil Service
Commission. The members of said commission shall be appointed by the Mayor
subject to confirmation by a majority of the council members. The initial terms
of members appointed to said board shall be staggered in compliance with the
provisions of Section
7.02 of this Charter. Thereafter, all appointments to the Civil Service
Commission shall be for a period of four (4) years.
Annotation—See KRS 67A.210 et seq., and Code of Ordinances
Chapter 21, relating to the classified civil service system.
Sec. 7.04. - Pension Fund Boards.
The Lexington Employees' Pension Fund Board and the Lexington Police and
Fireman's Pension Fund Board shall continue after the effective date of this
Charter as the Merged Government Employees' Pension Fund Board and the Merged
Government Police and Fireman's Pension Fund Board. Said boards shall continue
to administer the pension funds of all non-police and fire employees and all
police and fire employees of the Merged Government respectively under the
provisions and limitations of
Article Nine of this Charter governing employee pensions.
On the effective date of this Charter, the membership of the Merged Government
Employees' Pension Fund Board shall consist of the Mayor, four (4) members of
the Merged Government Council selected by the Council, the Commissioner of the
Department of Finance, the Director of the Division of Personnel and three (3)
civil service employees to be elected to the board by those employees covered
by the Employees' Pension Fund.
On the effective date of this Charter, the membership of the Merged Government
Police and Fireman's Pension Fund Board shall consist of the Mayor, the
Commissioner of the Department of Finance, the Director of the Division of
Personnel, the Director of the Division of Police, the Director of the Division
of Fire Protection, and two (2) elected representatives, one (1) from the
Division of Police and one (1) from the Division of Fire Protection.
Annotation—See KRS 67A.360-67A.690 relating to police and fire retirement. See
KRS 67A.320 and 67A.350 and Code of Ordinances
Chapter 6 relating to former city employees retirement.
Sec. 7.05. - Budget Commission.
The County Budget Commission, consisting of the County Judge, the County
Attorney, and one (1) member appointed by the Fiscal Court under the provisions
of Section
11.02 of this Charter, shall continue in full force and effect after the
effective date of this Charter until such time as the General Assembly of
Kentucky, or an appropriate state court, shall decide that, for purposes of
budgeting, the Lexington-Fayette Urban County Government is not a county under
the terms of the law governing county budgets. Until such time, the Budget
Commission of the Merged Government shall be responsible only for forwarding
the annual operating budget and capital improvements budget to the proper state
officer under law, and shall not have any responsibility for the preparation,
adoption or implementation of said budgets.
Annotation—"Statutes creating budget commissions are inapplicable to urban
county government". Holsclaw v. Stephens, supra, at 477.
Sec. 7.06. - Assessment Appeals.
The official board charged with hearing and deciding all assessment appeals in
the territory of the Merged Government shall be the Lexington-Fayette Urban
County Board of Supervisors. Said board shall be initially composed of the
members of the Fayette County Board of Supervisors and shall retain all of the
powers, duties and legal responsibilities of county boards of supervisors as
provided by law.
All vacancies on said board occurring after the effective date of this Charter
shall be filled by the County Judge in accordance with the provisions set forth
in Section
11.01 of this Charter. Members of the Board of Supervisors shall serve such
terms as may be prescribed by law for county boards of supervisors generally.
Annotation—The title of the board charged with hearing and deciding all
assessment appeals has been changed by KRS 133.120 to the board of assessment
appeals.
Sec. 7.07. - Civil Defense.
The Civil Defense Board of Advisors of the City of Lexington and the County of
Fayette shall continue after the effective date of this Charter as the
Lexington-Fayette Urban County Civil Defense Board of Advisors. Said board
shall advise the Director of the Division of Civil Defense in the Department of
Public Safety, formerly the Director of Civil Defense for Lexington and Fayette
County, on all matters pertaining to the operation and administration of a
civil defense program for the Merged Government. All vacancies on said board
occurring after the effective date of this Charter shall be filled by the
Mayor, subject to the provisions of Section
7.02 of this Charter.
Annotation—This board is no longer in existence. See Ordinances No. 136-88 and
23-90.
Sec. 7.08. - Parks and Recreation.
The Lexington Board of Parks Commissioners shall continue after the effective
date of this Charter as the Lexington-Fayette Urban County Board of Parks
Commissioners. Said board shall advise the Department of Parks and Recreation
on all matters pertaining to the operation and administration of all parks and
recreation programs of the Merged Government.
All vacancies occurring on said board after the effective date of this Charter
shall be filled by the Mayor, subject to the provisions of Section
7.02 of this Charter.
Annotation—The Urban County Government has not elected to operate under KRS
97.405 to 97.485. However, Code of Ordinances Section
2-396  et seq.; created the parks and recreation advisory board pursuant to KRS
67A.060 and 67A.070.
Sec. 7.09. - Homes for the Aged.
The Julius Marks Advisory Board, consisting of five (5) members, shall continue
after the effective date of this Charter. Said board shall advise the Director
of the Division of Homes of the Department of Social Services on all matters
pertaining to the operation and administration of the Julius Marks Home. It
shall be the particular responsibility of said advisory board to make periodic
inspections of the Julius Marks Home and to make such recommendations
concerning the care and treatment of the residents of said home as may be
deemed necessary.
All vacancies occurring after the effective date of this Charter shall be
filled by the Mayor, subject to the provisions of
7.02 of this Charter.
Annotation—The Julius Marks advisory board has been abolished. See Release of
record in Deed Book 1548, page 228 in the Fayette County Clerk's Office.
Sec. 7.10. - Social Services.
Pursuant to Section
7.01, the Executive Board of the Fayette County Children's Bureau shall be
terminated on the effective date of this Charter. In order to assure broad
citizen participation and involvement in the operation and management of the
total social services program of the Urban County Government, the members of
the former Executive Board of the Fayette County Children's Bureau shall
constitute a five-member Lexington-Fayette Urban County Social Services
Advisory Board. Said advisory board shall advise the Department of Social
Services on all matters pertaining to the operation, administration and
management of all welfare, domestic relations, juvenile and children's services
programs provided by the Urban County Government.
The terms of the original members of said board shall be equivalent to the
unexpired terms of the members of the former Executive Board of the Fayette
County Children's Bureau. All vacancies in said positions occurring after the
effective date of this Charter shall be filled by the Mayor in accordance with
the provisions of Section
7.02 of this Charter.
The Council shall, within ninety (90) days of the effective date of this
Charter, increase the size of the Social Services Advisory Board to nine (9)
members to be appointed in accordance with the provisions of Section
7.02 of this Charter.
Annotation—This section is invalid only "insofar as that section might be
construed to impinge upon the duties and membership of the Social Services
Advisory Committee created by KRS 205.330." Holsclaw v. Stephens, supra, at
481. Subsequently, KRS 205.330 was repealed.
Sec. 7.11. - Housing Appeals.
The Lexington Minimum Standard Housing Board of Appeals shall be continued
after the effective date of this Charter as the Lexington-Fayette Urban County
Minimum Standard Housing Board of Appeals. Said board shall exercise all of the
powers and functions under law of the former Lexington Minimum Standard Housing
Board of Appeals throughout the territory of the Merged Government and such
other duties and functions pertaining to the enforcement of minimum housing
codes as the Council may prescribe.
All vacancies on said board occurring after the effective date of this Charter
shall be filled by the Mayor, subject to the provisions of Section
7.02 of this Charter.
Annotation—This board was superseded by the administrative hearing board. See
Code of Ordinances Section
12-13.
Sec. 7.12. - Public Housing.
The Housing Authority of Lexington, or any successor authority created prior to
the effective date of this Charter, shall be continued after the effective date
of this Charter as the Lexington-Fayette Urban County Housing Authority. Said
authority shall retain all powers and authority as may be provided by law and
shall continue to plan, implement and administer all public housing programs
within the territorial limits of the Urban County Government.
On the effective date of this Charter, the Mayor of the Lexington-Fayette Urban
County Government shall replace the Mayor of the City of Lexington on said
authority. All other vacancies occurring after the effective date of said
Charter shall be filled by the Mayor in accordance with the provisions of KRS
80.030 to 80.060.
Sec. 7.13. - Urban Renewal.
The Lexington Urban Renewal and Community Development Agency shall be
terminated on the effective date of this Charter. Pursuant to KRS 99.330 to
99.510, the Lexington-Fayette Urban County Government shall be designated as a
"community." All powers, functions, rights, duties and privileges of an urban
renewal and community development "agency" shall be vested in said "community"
and shall be delegated to the Division of Urban Renewal in the Department of
Housing and Community Development in accordance with the provisions of KRS
99.490.
The members of the former Lexington Urban Renewal and Community Development
Agency shall constitute a five (5) member Urban Renewal Advisory Board. Said
board shall advise the Division of Urban Renewal, the Mayor and the Council on
all matters pertaining to urban renewal. All vacancies on said board occurring
after the effective date of this Charter shall be filled by the Mayor in
accordance with the provisions of Section
7.02 of this Charter.
Annotation—This section is invalid. Holsclaw v. Stephens, supra, at 479-480.
Sec. 7.14. - Planning Commission.
The Lexington-Fayette County Planning Commission shall continue after the
effective date of this Charter as the Lexington-Fayette Urban County Planning
Commission. Said commission shall take immediate steps to declare the
Lexington-Fayette Urban County Government as the official planning unit under
law to supersede the joint city-county agreement designating the City of
Lexington and the County of Fayette as an official planning unit.
Said commission shall have all the powers, duties and functions provided under
law for planning commissions generally. Pursuant to KRS 100.173, the Lexington-
Fayette Urban County Planning Commission shall utilize the Division of Planning
in the Department of Housing and Community Development for such professional
staff assistance as may be required to accomplish its assigned duties under
law.
All vacancies on the Lexington-Fayette Urban County Planning Commission
occurring after the effective date of this Charter shall be filled by the
Mayor, subject to the provisions of Section
7.02 of this Charter.
Sec. 7.15. - Zoning Adjustment.
The Lexington-Fayette County Board of Adjustment shall continue after the
effective date of this Charter as the Lexington-Fayette Urban County Board of
Adjustment. Said board shall have all the powers, duties and functions provided
under law for boards of adjustment generally. Pursuant to KRS 100.223, the
Lexington-Fayette Urban County Board of Adjustment shall utilize the Division
of Planning in the Department of Housing and Community Development for such
professional staff assistance as may be required to accomplish its assigned
duties under law.
All vacancies on the Lexington-Fayette Urban County Board of Adjustment shall
be filled by the Mayor, subject to the provision of Section
7.02 of this Charter.
Sec. 7.16. - Board of Health.
The Lexington-Fayette County Board of Health shall continue after the effective
date of this Charter as the Lexington-Fayette Urban County Board of Health.
Said board shall retain all of the powers, duties and functions under law as
may be now or hereafter assigned to county boards of health, and shall continue
to supervise and direct the activities of the City-County Health Department as
provided by law. The Director and staff of the Urban County Health Department
shall continue to be appointed in accordance with the provisions of applicable
state law.
On the effective date of this Charter, the Mayor, as the Chief Executive
Officer of the Merged Government, shall replace the County Judge as an ex-
officio member of the health board. On said date, the Lexington City Manager
shall be replaced as an ex-officio member of the board by a person appointed by
the Council of the Merged Government in accordance with the provisions of state
law pertaining to the composition of county health boards generally. All other
members of the board on the effective date of this Charter shall continue to
serve until such time as their terms are completed and their successors are
appointed. All vacancies on said board after the effective date of this Charter
shall be made in accordance with applicable state law.
Annotation—See KRS 212.627, which was adopted after the Charter went into
effect.
Sec. 7.17. - Human Rights Commission.
The Lexington-Fayette County Human Rights Commission shall continue after the
effective date of this Charter as the Lexington-Fayette Urban County Human
Rights Commission. Said commission shall retain all of the powers, duties and
functions under law as may be now or hereafter assigned to commissions on human
rights generally. The Lexington-Fayette Urban County Human Rights Commission
shall retain all powers pertaining to the appointment of an executive director
and staff as prescribed by law.
All vacancies on said commission occurring after the effective date of this
Charter shall be filled by the Mayor, subject to the provisions of Section
7.02 of this Charter.
Annotation—See KRS 344.320 and Code of Ordinances Section
2-25  et seq.
Sec. 7.18. - Airport Board.
The Lexington-Fayette County Airport Board shall continue after the effective
date of this Charter as the Lexington-Fayette Urban County Airport Board. Said
board shall retain all of the powers, duties and functions under law as may be
now or hereafter assigned to city, county or joint city-county airport boards.
The Lexington-Fayette Urban Airport Board shall retain all powers pertaining to
the appointment of an airport manager and staff as prescribed by law.
All vacancies on said board occurring after the effective date of this Charter
shall be appointed by the Mayor, subject to the provisions of Section
7.02 of this Charter.
Annotation—See KRS 183.132 and Code of Ordinances
Chapter 2A.
Sec. 7.19. - Library Board.
The Lexington Library Board of Trustees shall continue after the effective date
of this Charter as the Lexington-Fayette Urban County Library Board of
Trustees. Said board shall retain all powers, duties and functions as may be
now or hereafter prescribed by law governing the operation of public libraries
by cities of the second class. The Lexington-Fayette Urban County Library Board
of Trustees shall retain all powers pertaining to the appointment of a
librarian, assistant librarian and staff as prescribed by law. All vacancies on
said board occurring after the effective date of this Charter shall be filled
by the Mayor, subject to the provisions of Section
7.02 of this Charter.
The Lexington Public Library Board of Advisors shall continue after the
effective date of this Charter, and shall be charged with advising the Mayor
and the Library Board of Trustees on all matters pertaining to the operation
and administration of public library services for the Merged Government. All
vacancies on said board of advisors shall be filled by the Mayor, subject to
the provisions of Section
7.02 of this Charter.
Annotation—See KRS 173.350. In Lexington-Fayette Urban County Government v.
Hayse, Ky.App., 684 S.W.2d 301 (1985), it was held that the library must be
funded consistent with KRS 173.360(1).
Sec. 7.20. - Transit Authority.
The Transit Authority of the City of Lexington and the County of Fayette shall
continue in full force and effect after the effective date of this Charter as
the Transit Authority of the Lexington-Fayette Urban County Government. Said
authority shall retain all the power and authority vested therein by ordinance
and resolution of the Board of Commissioners of the City of Lexington and the
Fayette County Fiscal Court on the effective date of this Charter, and shall
continue to be responsible for fulfilling the mass transportation needs of the
citizens of the Merged Government.
All vacancies on said authority occurring after the effective date of this
Charter shall be filled by the Mayor in accordance with the provisions of
Section
7.02 of this Charter.
Annotation—See KRS 96A.020.
ARTICLE 8. - BUDGET AND FINANCIAL MATTERS
Sec. 8.01. - Fiscal Year.
The fiscal year of the Merged Government shall begin on the first day of July
of each year and shall end on the thirtieth day of June next following. Said
fiscal year shall constitute the budget year and the year for all financial
accounting and reporting for every office, department, agency, board and
commission of the Merged Government. The aforementioned provision shall be in
addition to, and not in lieu of, any accounting or reporting requirements
affecting any official or agency of the Merged Government by state or federal
laws.
Sec. 8.02. - Budget Preparation.
The Merged Government Council shall prescribe, by ordinance, the procedures and
requirements for the preparation, adoption and execution of an annual operating
and an annual capital improvements budget. Said ordinance shall require the use
of program budgeting by the Merged Government, and shall be consistent with the
budgetary provisions of Sections
5.04 and
5.10 of this Charter.
It shall be the duty of all officers, departments, agencies, boards and
commissions receiving appropriations from the Merged Government to furnish the
Chief Administrative Officer and the Mayor such information as may be required
to prepare the annual operating and capital improvements budgets.
Subject to the provisions of Section
5.04 of this Charter, the Mayor shall submit the proposed annual operating and
capital improvements budgets to the Council on or before a date fixed by
ordinance, but not less than sixty (60) days prior to the beginning of the next
fiscal year. Said budgets shall be accompanied by a budget message from the
Mayor containing explanations of general fiscal policies, major changes
recommended for the next fiscal year and notification of those points at which
the budgetary recommendations of the Chief Administrative Officer are at
variance with those submitted by the Mayor. Copies of the budgets shall be
filed with the County Clerk and shall be open to public inspection. A summary
of the proposed budgets shall be published in one (1) or more newspapers of
general circulation within the territory of the Merged Government not less than
seven (7) days prior to their adoption by the Council.
Annotation—See Ordinances No. 39-75 and 1-76.
Sec. 8.03. - Scope of the Budgets.
The annual operating and capital improvements budgets shall consist of two (2)
parts. Part I of the annual operating and capital improvements budgets shall
set forth, in detail, the revenue, expenditures, and program information for
those services, functions, activities and capital improvements projects
pertaining to the General Services District.
Part II of the annual operating and capital improvements budgets shall set
forth, in detail, the revenues, expenditures, and program information for those
services, functions, activities and capital improvements projects pertaining to
the Full Urban Services District and such Partial Urban Services Districts as
may be created and established by the Council.
Each of the above described parts of the annual operating budget shall contain,
with respect to each of the operating funds of the Merged Government to which
they are applicable: a) an estimate of the encumbered fund balance for the
remainder of the current fiscal year; b) a reasonable estimate of cash revenues
to be received during the next fiscal year, classified according to source; c)
proposed expenditures detailed by each office, department, agency, and activity
in accordance with an established classification of accounts, including those
capital outlays which are to be financed from the revenues of the next year; d)
insurance and pension costs and all debt service requirements for said fiscal
year payable from such funds; e) work programs and performance data in
justification of proposed expenditures; and f) such other information as may be
considered necessary or as may be desired by the Mayor or Council.
Parts I and II of the annual capital improvements budget shall contain: a) an
estimate of the encumbered capital improvements fund balance for the remainder
of the current fiscal year; b) a description of all planned capital
improvements to be funded during the next fiscal year; c) the amount and source
of all capital improvements expenditures for the next fiscal year; d) a
detailed summary of the capital improvements program planned for the next five
(5) fiscal years indicating the projected costs and sources of revenue for each
separate project, purpose, facility or other capital improvement covered in the
five-year program; and e) a copy of any studies and surveys pertaining to the
contents of the annual capital improvements budget.
Sec. 8.04. - Adoption of the Annual Operating Budget.
The Council shall, upon receipt of the annual operating budget from the Mayor,
schedule and hold one (1) or more public hearings on the contents of the
budget. Notice shall be published in a newspaper of general circulation in the
territory of the Merged Government at least seven (7) days prior to the date
set for such hearings.
The Council may amend the proposed annual operating budget submitted by the
Mayor, except that the budget, as amended and adopted, shall provide for all
expenditures required by law or by other provisions of this Charter, and for
all debt service requirements for the next fiscal year.
Adoption of the annual operating budget by the Council shall be in the form of
an annual appropriation ordinance. Said ordinance shall be adopted by the
Council and forwarded to the Mayor not later than the fifteenth day of June
each year. In the event that final action on the annual operating budget
ordinance, including Council action on any veto or item veto by the Mayor, is
not completed by the thirtieth day of June each year, the amounts appropriated
for operations for the fiscal year just ended shall be deemed adopted for the
current fiscal year on a month-to-month basis, with all items prorated
accordingly until such time as the Council shall complete action on the
appropriation ordinance for the annual operating budget for the current fiscal
year.
The appropriations ordinance for the annual operating budget shall specify
estimated revenues by source and shall list all appropriations according to
fund by organizational unit, purpose or activity as set forth in the format of
the budget document submitted by the Mayor. The amount set forth in the
appropriation ordinance for each organizational unit, purpose or activity shall
constitute the annual appropriation for such item.
The Council may, by vote of three-fifths ( 3/5 ) of its membership, make
additional appropriations to the Merged Government during any fiscal year,
provided that the additional funds are derived from unappropriated funds. In
addition, the Council may, by a majority vote of its members, empower the Mayor
to transfer the unencumbered balance of any appropriation, or portion thereof,
to another appropriation category within the same section of the budget and
within the same fund. In no case shall the Council authorize the transfer of
funds from one services district appropriation to another as specified in Parts
I and II of the annual operating budget.
Sec. 8.05. - Adoption of the Annual Capital Improvements Budget.
The Council shall, upon receipt of the annual capital improvements budget from
the Mayor, schedule one (1) or more public hearings on the contents of said
budget. The Council may, however, schedule such hearings on the annual capital
improvements budget concurrently with those scheduled to hear testimony on the
annual operating budget. Notice of hearings shall be published in a newspaper
of general circulation in the territory of the Merged Government at least seven
(7) days prior to the date set for such hearings.
The Council may delete projects from the annual capital improvements budget as
submitted to it by the Mayor, but shall not otherwise amend said budget until
it has requested in writing the recommendations of the Mayor and the Chief
Administrative Officer concerning any proposed amendment the Council intends to
make. The Council may specify a time limit of not less than five (5) days
within which the Mayor and the Chief Administrative Officer may provide written
recommendations. The Council shall not be bound by such written
recommendations, and may act without them if they are not received within the
time limit specified by the Council.
Adoption of the annual capital improvements budget by the Council shall be in
the form of an annual capital improvements ordinance which shall specify the
capital improvements to be made during the next fiscal year and the contents of
the capital improvements program planned for the next five (5) fiscal years.
Said ordinance shall be adopted by the Council and forwarded to the Mayor not
later than the fifteenth day of June each year. Final action on the annual
capital improvements ordinance, including Council action on any veto by the
Mayor, shall be completed by the thirtieth day of June each year.
All appropriations for capital improvements expenditures for the next fiscal
year shall be included in the annual operating appropriations ordinance. Said
appropriations by the Council shall be in conformity with that part of the
annual capital improvements program applicable to the next fiscal year; and
shall be consistent with the descriptions of proposed expenditures, sources of
revenue and type of capital improvements to be made during that fiscal year as
set forth in the annual capital improvements ordinance.
Sec. 8.06. - Levy of Taxes.
Following the final adoption of the annual operating appropriation ordinance on
or before the thirtieth day of June each year, the Council shall:
(a)   Levy, by ordinance, an ad valorem tax on all properties, real and
personal, within the General Services District as are now or hereafter may be
subject to such taxation by counties containing cities of the second class
under the Constitution and laws of the Commonwealth of Kentucky. The rates set
by ordinance for the ad valorem tax on property within said services district
shall not exceed those established by the Constitution and laws of the
Commonwealth of Kentucky for counties containing cities of the second class,
and shall be consistent with the provisions of this Charter governing ad
valorem taxes within the General Services District. In addition, said tax rates
shall be based on a reasonable estimate of the cash revenues required from ad
valorem property taxes to cover those appropriations made under Part I of the
annual operating and capital improvements budget ordinances for the General
Services District.
(b)   Levy, by ordinance, an additional ad valorem tax on all properties, real
and personal, within the Full Urban Services District and such Partial Urban
Services Districts as may be created or established by the Council as are now
or hereafter may be subject to such taxation by cities of the second class
under the Constitution and laws of the Commonwealth of Kentucky. The rates set
by ordinance for the additional ad valorem tax on property within said services
districts shall not exceed those established by the Constitution and laws of
the Commonwealth of Kentucky for cities of the second class, and shall be
consistent with the provisions of this Charter governing ad valorem taxes
within the Full Urban Services District and Partial Urban Services Districts.
In addition, said tax rates shall be based on a reasonable estimate of the cash
revenues required from ad valorem property taxes to cover those appropriations
made under Part II of the annual operating and capital improvements budgets or
ordinances for the Full Urban Services and Partial Urban Services Districts not
covered by the ad valorem tax imposed on property within said districts under
the provisions of this Charter governing the General Services District.
(c)   Levy, by ordinance, such other taxes as are now or hereafter may be
levied by counties containing cities of the second class or by cities of the
second class themselves under the Constitution and laws of the Commonwealth of
Kentucky as may be required to meet the annual appropriations for the General
Services District, the Full Urban Services District and such Partial Urban
Services Districts as the Council may create. All tax levies made under this
section shall be uniform throughout the territorial limits of the Merged
Government, and shall be based on a reasonable estimate of the cash revenues
required to cover the appropriations made under Parts I and II of the annual
operating and capital improvements budget ordinances not covered or anticipated
by the levy of the ad valorem tax imposed on property located within the
General Services District, the Full Urban Services District, or such Partial
Urban Services Districts as may be created by the Council.
The Merged Government Council shall provide, by ordinance, for the manner and
method of collecting all delinquent taxes due the Merged Government as may be
consistent with, the laws of Kentucky.
Annotation—The enabling legislation for ad valorem property taxes is KRS
67A.850 and for occupational license fees is KRS 67A.060, 67A.070(1), 92.280(2)
and 92.281. The ad valorem tax on real property may be raised only in
accordance with KRS 132.027 and the ad valorem tax on personal property is
limited by KRS 132.029. See also note at Section
2.01.
Sec. 8.07. - Homestead Exemptions.
All homestead exemptions provided under the Constitution and laws of the
Commonwealth of Kentucky presently in force, or as may be hereafter provided,
shall be applicable to all property located within the territorial limits of
the Merged Government.
Sec. 8.08. - Independent Audit.
An annual independent audit of such accounts and other evidences of financial
transactions of the Merged Government shall be performed as the Council may
determine; provided that said audit shall be made by an accountant or
accounting firm that does not have any pecuniary, personal or other interest,
direct or indirect, in the fiscal affairs of the Merged Government or any of
its offices, departments, agencies, boards and commissions. Said audit shall be
completed not later than four (4) months after the close of the fiscal year,
and shall be made public in a manner prescribed by the Council. In addition,
the Council may, at any time, order an independent audit of any office,
department, agency, board or commission of the Merged Government, provided that
the Council gives adequate notice of its intent to do so.
Sec. 8.09. - Borrowing and Indebtedness.
The Lexington-Fayette Urban County Government may issue any bonds which
counties containing a city of the second class or cities of the second class
are, or hereafter may be, authorized to issue under the Constitution and laws
of the Commonwealth of Kentucky. All bonds issued by the Merged Government
after the effective date of this Charter shall be allocated to the General
Services District, the Full Urban Services District, or any Partial Urban
Services Districts for the purpose of funding services rendered by the Merged
Government in said districts.
All bonds issued before the effective date of this Charter by the County of
Fayette and all bonds authorized but unissued by the County of Fayette on the
effective date of this Charter shall be allocated to the General Services
District. All bonds issued before the effective date of this Charter by the
City of Lexington and all bonds authorized but unissued by the City of
Lexington on the effective date of this Charter shall be allocated to the Full
Urban Services District.
Sec. 8.10. - General Obligation and Revenue Bonds.
All general obligation bonds shall be issued in the name of the Lexington-
Fayette Urban County Government and shall be an obligation thereof. The full
faith and credit of the Merged Government shall be pledged for all general
obligation bonds issued under the provisions of this Charter.
The Council of the Merged Government is hereby empowered and authorized to
issue revenue bonds for the purpose and manner as now or hereafter may be
provided under the general laws of Kentucky governing counties or cities of the
second class.
All revenue derived by the Merged Government from the issuance and sale of
bonds shall be used exclusively for the purposes for which such bonds were
issued, and all taxes or other revenues collected for the purpose of servicing
or retiring such bonds shall be used exclusively for the payment of principal
and interest thereof.
Sec. 8.11. - Debt Service and Debt Limitation.
There shall be a Debt Service Fund for each services district established by
this Charter, or by ordinance pursuant thereto, for the amortization of the
respective bonds issued for each services district, including bonds issued
prior to the effective date of this Charter by either the City of Lexington or
the County of Fayette allocated to any particular services district under the
terms of this Charter. All debt service funds, or their equivalent, for bonds
issued by the City of Lexington or the County of Fayette prior to the effective
date of this Charter shall be transferred to the Debt Service Fund of the
services district to which such bonds are allocated by this Charter.
For purposes of computing the legal debt limitations applicable to the
Lexington-Fayette Urban County Government under the Constitution and laws of
the Commonwealth of Kentucky, the following definitions shall apply:
(a)   The General Services District shall be construed as a county containing a
city of the second class.
(b)   The area embraced by the Full Urban Services District, plus the area
embraced by all Partial Urban Services Districts created under the terms of
this Charter, shall be construed as a city of the second class.
ARTICLE 9. - PERSONNEL AND PENSION SYSTEMS 4
 
Notes
  Annotation—See KRS 67A.200 et seq. , and 95.435 et seq. , and Code of
  Ordinances Chapters
4 6,
  21,
  22 and
  23, relating to the personnel and pension systems.
Sec. 9.01. - General.
It shall be the policy of the Lexington-Fayette Urban County Government to
hire, promote and compensate all employees without regard to race, sex, creed
or national origin.
Sec. 9.02. - The Classified Civil Service.
All positions in the Lexington-Fayette Urban County Government shall be in the
classified civil service except:
A.   Officers elected by the voters, and persons appointed to fill vacancies in
elective offices;
B.   Members of all boards, commissions and authorities established under the
provisions of this Charter or by ordinance pursuant thereto;
C.   The Chief Administrative Officer;
D.   Department Commissioners of all executive departments created by this
Charter or by ordinance pursuant thereto;
E.   All administrative assistants appointed by the Mayor under the provisions
of Section
5.08 of this Charter and all secretaries so excluded by the provisions of said
section;
F.   Temporary or part-time employees and all persons employed to conduct
special inquiries, investigations or studies for the Merged Government.
Sec. 9.03. - Rules and Regulations Governing the Classified Civil Service.
Subject to the provisions of Section
9.02 of this Charter, all rules and regulations pertaining to the classified
civil service set forth in
Chapter Six of the "Code of Ordinances, City of Lexington, Kentucky" on the
effective date of this Charter shall continue in full force and effect. Said
rules and regulations shall remain in effect until such time as the Council
adopts by ordinance a comprehensive classified civil service plan for the
Lexington-Fayette Urban County Government.
Subject to the limitations set forth in Section
9.02, all employees of the City of Lexington and the County of Fayette not
covered by the above rules and regulations on the effective date of this
Charter shall be placed under the classified civil service at a classification
level commensurate with the kind and type of duties assigned to said employees
by the City of Lexington or the County of Fayette immediately prior to the
effective date of this Charter. In no case shall any employee placed under the
classified civil service in accordance with this provision receive a salary or
wage lower than that received on the effective date of this Charter. Nor shall
any such employee be subject to any examination or certification requirements
except those pertaining to promotion or change of classification after their
initial entry into the classified civil service.
Sec. 9.04. - Adoption of a Classified Civil Service Plan for the Merged
Government.
As soon as practical, but not more than two (2) years after the effective date
of this Charter, the Division of Personnel in the Office of Administrative
Services shall prepare and submit to the Mayor and the Chief Administrative
Officer a comprehensive plan for a classified civil service system for the
Lexington-Fayette Urban County Government. Said plan shall then be submitted to
the Council along with such written recommendations as the Mayor and the Chief
Administrative Officer may wish to make. Among other things, the aforementioned
plan shall provide for:
(a)   The position classification of all positions in the classified civil
service;
(b)   The procedures for recruiting, examining and certifying all candidates
for positions in the classified civil service;
(c)   The method and procedure for promoting persons in the classified civil
service;
(d)   The rules governing hours of work, vacations, sick leave, leaves of
absence, layoffs, suspension and other disciplinary actions, in-service
training, employee salaries and benefits; and
(e)   Such other provisions as may be necessary for the efficient operation and
administration of the classified civil service.
Adoption of the comprehensive classified civil service plan shall be by
ordinance passed by the Council. All subsequent additions, revisions or
amendments affecting the classified civil service shall be made by ordinance.
In no case shall the Council initiate or enact any such additions, revisions or
amendments without first securing the written recommendations of the Mayor, the
Chief Administrative Officer and the Director of the Division of Personnel.
Pursuant to Section
7.03 of this Charter, the Division of Personnel shall consult with and seek the
advice of the Civil Service Commission on all matters pertaining to the
preparation, adoption and subsequent revision of the comprehensive classified
civil service plan for the Merged Government.
Sec. 9.05. - Administration of the Classified Civil Service.
Pursuant to the provisions of Section
6.04 of this Charter, the Division of Personnel in the Office of Administrative
Services shall be responsible for the administration of all ordinances and
regulations pertaining to the classified civil service, including all
recruitment, examination, classification, probation, promotion and compensation
programs affecting the classified civil service.
The Civil Service Commission, in accordance with the provisions of Section
7.03 of this Charter, shall advise the Division of Personnel on all matters
pertaining to the management and administration of the classified civil
service, and shall officially certify all applicants to be placed on the list
of qualified persons eligible for positions in the classified civil service.
Said commission shall also hear and decide, subject to appeal as provided in
Chapter Six of the Code of Ordinances for the City of Lexington or ordinance
passed by the Council of the Merged Government in pursuance of this Charter,
all cases involving the suspension, dismissal or other disciplinary actions
brought against employees covered by the classified civil service provisions of
this Charter.
Sec. 9.06. - The Unclassified Civil Service.
Except as otherwise provided in this Charter, the Council shall establish by
ordinance the qualifications, compensation and other terms of employment for
all employees exempted from the classified civil service.
All temporary or part-time employees of the City of Lexington and the County of
Fayette not covered by the provisions of this Charter pertaining to the
classified civil service on the effective date of this Charter shall be
retained for a period of sixty (60) days. Thereafter, said employees shall be
retained only by affirmative action by the Council on recommendation of the
Chief Administrative Officer and the Director of the Division of Personnel.
The Division of Personnel shall administer all ordinances and regulations
pertaining to the employment and compensation of persons exempted from the
classified civil service under the terms of this Charter.
Sec. 9.07. - Employee Pension Plans Continued.
All pension and retirement plans of the City of Lexington existing on the
effective date of this Charter shall continue in full force and effect. All
benefits and rights provided by said plans shall continue unimpaired and shall
constitute an obligation and liability of the Lexington-Fayette Urban County
Government. The Council may, within the limits of law, increase the rights and
benefits of said plans, but may not decrease such rights and benefits.
All persons entitled to benefits under the aforementioned pension plans on the
effective date of this Charter shall continue to be entitled to such benefits.
After the effective date of this Charter, service with the Merged Government
shall constitute service under the terms and provisions of said plans for the
purpose of determining eligibility of benefits. In no case shall any employees
of the Merged Government be entitled to benefits under said plans unless they
are a member thereof.
Sec. 9.08. - Membership in Pension Plans.
All members of the police and firemen and other employee pension plans of the
City of Lexington on the effective date of this Charter shall continue as
members of said plans unless otherwise specifically exempted therefrom under
the provisions of this Charter. All new employees entering the classified civil
service of the Merged Government after the effective date of this Charter shall
be enrolled as members of the police and firemen or other employee pension plan
in accordance with the terms and conditions for membership therein. No other
employee, including those employees of the City of Lexington and County of
Fayette entering the classified civil service of the Merged Government in
accordance with the provisions of Section
9.03 of this Charter, shall be eligible for membership in said pension plans
until the Council has provided by ordinance for the terms and conditions to be
applied in extending the membership of any pension plan beyond the limits set
forth in this Charter.
In no case shall the Council extend the membership in any pension plan beyond
the limits set forth in this Charter that will result in the impairment,
curtailment or diminishment of any right or benefit accrued by any person who
is a member of said plan on the effective date of this Charter. Nor shall the
Council extend membership in any pension plan to any employee of the Merged
Government exempted from the classified civil service. However, the Council may
provide by ordinance for the continuation of membership in any pension plan for
any classified civil service employee appointed as an Administrative Assistant
to the Mayor or as a Department Commissioner under the provisions of Sections
5.08 or
6.02 of this Charter.
Annotation—Under KRS 78.510(6), 78.531 and 78.540 every regular full-time
appointed or elective officer or employee, except members of the Policemen's
and Fire Fighter's Retirement Fund and City Employees Pension Fund, of an urban
county government participating in the County Employees Retirement System must
be included in the membership of that fund. The Lexington-Fayette Urban County
Government is a participant in the County Employees Retirement System, so full-
time non-classified civil service employees are covered by the pension plan.
Sec. 9.09. - Administration of Pension Plans.
Pursuant to Section
6.04 of this Charter, the Division of Personnel in the Office of Administrative
Services shall administer all employee pension and retirement programs of the
Merged Government. All decisions concerning the management, investment and
administration of the pension funds for police and firemen and other employees
shall be made by the appropriate pension fund board designated in Section
7.04 of this Charter.
Sec. 9.10. - Other Retirement Systems.
The Council is hereby authorized and empowered to establish and provide such
other pension systems, Social Security programs or other retirement benefits
allowable under law as may be deemed necessary or desirable for those employees
not covered by the pension provisions of Sections
9.07 and
9.08 of this Charter.
Sec. 9.11. - Construction.
Except as otherwise provided in this Charter, the Council shall have the power
to establish, delegate and otherwise provide for the operation and
administration of all policies pertaining to the employment, compensation and
fringe benefits of all employees of the Merged Government.
ARTICLE 10. - URBAN COUNTY COURTS 5
 
Notes
5 Annotation—The structure of the local court system was modified by Kentucky
  Constitution Sections 109-124, effective January 1, 1976.
Sec. 10.01. - General.
The courts of the Lexington-Fayette Urban County Government shall consist of a
Quarterly Court, a County Court, and three (3) Justices' Courts. The Municipal
Court of the City of Lexington shall be terminated thirty (30) days after the
effective date of this Charter; and all powers, duties and jurisdictional
authority of said Court shall be vested in the Urban County Courts and such
other Courts as the laws of Kentucky may now, or hereafter, provide.
Annotation—The provision delaying the termination of the municipal court until
thirty days after the effective date of the Charter was held invalid. The
effect of this ruling was that the former police court of the City of Lexington
was terminated as of the effective date of the Charter on January 1, 1974,
rather than thirty days later. Holsclaw v. Stephens, supra, at 480-481.
Sec. 10.02. - Status of the Circuit Courts.
The Circuit Courts in and for the County of Fayette shall continue without
interruption resulting from the adoption of this Charter, and nothing herein
shall be construed as affecting the legal jurisdiction of said Courts. The
Judges of said Courts shall submit all requests for annual operating funds,
above and beyond those items covered by fees and emoluments provided by law, to
the Merged Government in accordance with the provisions of
Article Eight of this Charter. All other legal provisions pertaining to the
relationship between Circuit Courts and Counties on the date this Charter is
put into effect shall be maintained between said Courts and the Urban County
Government.
Sec. 10.03. - Quarterly Court.
The Quarterly Court of Fayette County, as constituted under the Constitution
and laws of the Commonwealth of Kentucky on the effective date of this Charter,
shall continue in full force and effect. The Judge of said Court shall be the
County Judge as provided in Section
11.01 of this Charter. Said Court shall be organized into a Civil Division, a
Criminal Division, a Traffic Division, and such other divisions as the County
Judge may from time to time deem necessary. The Judge of the Quarterly Court
shall appoint such Trial Commissioners as may be authorized and funded by the
Council of the Merged Government to handle the case load of the Quarterly Court
or its various divisions.
Sec. 10.04. - County Court.
The County Court of Fayette County, as constituted under the Constitution and
laws of the Commonwealth of Kentucky on the effective date of this Charter,
shall continue in full force and effect. The Judge of said Court shall be the
County Judge as provided in Section
11.01 of this Charter. Said Court shall be organized into a Probate Division, a
Juvenile Division, and such other divisions as the County Judge may from time
to time deem necessary. The Judge of the County Court shall appoint such Trial
Commissioners as may be authorized and funded by the Council of the Merged
Government to handle the case load of the County Court or its various
divisions.
Sec. 10.05. - Justices' Courts.
The Justices' Courts, as constituted and operated in Fayette County under the
