ARTICLE XXX. - GREENSPACE TRUST 16
 
Notes
   Editor's note(s)—Ord. No. 073-2022 , §§ 1—9, repealed §§ 2-326—2-334 and Ord. No. 075-
   2022 repealed §§ 2-335—2-340 and enacted a new art. XXX, §§
   2-335—2-340 as set out herein. Former art. XXX pertained to the Greenspace Commission
16 and derived from Ord. No. 264-90, § 1, adopted December 6, 1990; Ord. No. 139-93, § 1,
   adopted July 8, 1993; Ord. No. 295-2002, § 1, adopted November 21, 2002; Ord. No. 313-
   2002, § 1, adopted December 5, 2002; Ord. No. 210-2004, § 1, adopted August 26, 2004;
   and Ord. No. 53-2007, § 1, adopted March 22, 2007.
Sec. 2-335. - Definitions.
As used in this chapter, the following terms shall have the meanings indicated:
(1)   Application shall mean the documentation and information submitted to the
Greenspace Trust staff by a landowner on the approved application form offering
to transfer to the Greenspace Trust or the Lexington-Fayette Urban County
Government a conservation easement in eligible land.
(2)   Comprehensive plan shall mean the land use plan, and amendments thereto,
adopted by the Lexington-Fayette Urban County Government pursuant to KRS
100.197.
(3)   Conservation easement shall mean a non-possessory interest in real
property, which is acquired in perpetuity for the purpose of retaining and
enhancing greenspace within the urban service boundary or expansion areas;
preserving natural, scenic, open space or greenspace values of real property;
preserving areas or structures of architectural or historical interest; or
other like or similar purposes.
(4)   Greenspace shall mean open-space areas reserved for parks and other
"green spaces", including plant life, water features - also referred to as blue
spaces - and other kinds of natural environment.
(5)   Greenspace management plan shall mean the element of the comprehensive
plan adopted by the planning commission of the Lexington-Fayette Urban County
Government and shall include any future portions of the comprehensive plan, and
amendments thereto, pertaining to the urban service and expansion areas.
(6)   Greenspace Trust staff shall mean the personnel within the Lexington-
Fayette Urban County Government charged by the council with the duty to
administer this trust.
(7)   Reserved.
(Ord. No. 075-2022 , § 1, 7-7-22)
Sec. 2-336. - Organization; purpose.
(1)   Horst Schach and Fred Duerson, both being residents of Fayette County,
are hereby authorized and requested to serve as incorporators for and to
organize a non-profit, nonstock Kentucky corporation under the provisions of
Chapter 273 of the Kentucky Revised Statutes to be named "Lexington-Fayette
Urban County Greenspace Trust, Inc." and hereinafter referred to as the
"Greenspace Trust."
(2)   The purpose of the Greenspace Trust is to (1) preserve, maintain and
enhance the county's unique and special character for the economic, education
and general health, safety and welfare of the citizens; (2) apply for and
receive funds, contributions and donations, to further the purposes of the
Greenspace Trust, including donation of real property and easements; (3) to
develop a comprehensive greenspace management plan; and (4) to preserve,
protect and enhance open space in the urban service and expansion area(s).
(3)   The Greenspace Trust is enabled to:
(a)   Identify the following resources and seek to protect and preserve them
and, where appropriate, to enhance them:
I.   Those greenspaces within the county which possess the characteristics
which give the Bluegrass Region its unique identity;
II.   Those visual elements (scenic areas, scenic vistas, and scenic corridors)
which contribute to the unique scenic beauty of the Bluegrass Region;
III.   Those elements of our historic and cultural heritage as they exist in
relation to greenspace;
IV.   Natural areas;
V.   Environmentally sensitive areas;
VI.   Geologically hazardous areas;
VII.   Greenspace for passive recreational use, including, parkways, and
greenways;
VIII.   Water resources.
(b)   Utilize and manage greenspace in a comprehensive and systematic manner
which shall:
I.   Shape and reinforce the urban service area concept;
II.   Encourage more efficient and sensitive use of the land, improving the
quality of life and landscape, by providing patterns for development, hence,
making development and conservation of open space mutually beneficial;
III.   Help achieve an ecologically sustainable relationship between humans and
their uses and the environment;
IV.   Stimulate economic growth by channeling and encouraging development in a
manner conducive to the preservation of the character of this region;
V.   Strengthen tourism and related business and attract new businesses through
the preservation of our unique character; and
VI.   Provide an accessible system of open spaces which offer significant
educational value and opportunities.
(c)   Encourage cooperation and communication with surrounding counties as
regards the promotion of greenspace, protection of the environment, and land
conservation.
(Ord. No. 075-2022 , § 2, 7-7-22)
Sec. 2-337. - Board; membership.
(1)   The Greenspace Trust shall consist of eighteen (18) members. Fifteen (15)
members shall be voting members and three (3) shall be ex-officio non-voting
members.
(2)   The fifteen (15) voting members shall work or live in Fayette County and
shall have demonstrated an interest in greenspace; conservation of natural
areas and; protecting and preserving the Bluegrass Region unique
characteristics.
(3)   Three (3) non-voting members shall be ex-officio, members of the
Greenspace Trust and shall consist of the following positions:
(a)   One (1) designee from the Urban County Division of Parks and Recreation;
(b)   One (1) designee from the Urban County Division of Planning;
(c)   One (1) designee from Urban County Division of Environmental Quality and
Public Works.
(4)   All voting members shall work or live in Fayette County with a
demonstrated interest in the purposes and goals of the Greenspace Trust and
shall be appointed by the mayor and approved by majority vote of the urban
county council. The members of the Greenspace Trust shall serve without
compensation but shall be reimbursed for expenses necessarily incurred in the
performance of their duties.
(Ord. No. 075-2022 , § 3, 7-7-22)
Sec. 2-338. - Terms of board members.
(1)   All board members shall serve two (2) years from the date of appointment,
provided that the terms shall be staggered in the manner required by section
7.02 of the Urban County Charter. Vacancies shall be filled for the unexpired
term in the manner prescribed for the original appointment. Any Greenspace
Trust member may be reappointed for additional terms.
(2)   Vacancies in the voting membership shall be filled for an unexpired term
in the manner prescribed for the original appointment. The membership of the ex
officio non-voting members shall be terminated upon leaving the specified
offices.
(3)   A voting member of the Greenspace Trust shall be removed only by a
majority vote of the council, and only for cause, except that a member of the
board shall automatically be removed by operation of law in the event of three
(3) unexcused absences, whether consecutive or non-consecutive, in any two (2)
year period or in the event of absence from twenty-five (25) percent of the
meetings in any two (2) year period. An unexcused absence is any absence in
which the chair of the board or the Greenspace Trust staff is not notified of
the intended absence at least twenty-four (24) hours in advance of a regularly
scheduled meeting. In the event of three (3) unexcused absences or the absence
from twenty-five (25) percent of the meetings over any two (2) year period,
within the meaning of this section, the Greenspace Trust staff shall notify the
mayor and council administrator that a vacancy exists on the Greenspace Trust.
(Ord. No. 075-2022 , § 4, 7-7-22)
Sec. 2-339. - Board; officers; quorum; staff.
(1)   The officers of the Greenspace Trust shall consist of a chair, a vice-
chair, and other officers elected from the membership as set forth in the
bylaws. They shall take office at the first meeting of the Greenspace Trust
after their election. The duties of the officers shall be as specified in the
bylaws. The Greenspace Trust shall determine its own rules and order of
business and so provide for keeping a record of its proceedings.
(2)   A majority of the voting members of the Greenspace Trust, shall
constitute a quorum for transaction of business at any meeting of the
Greenspace Trust. The acts of a majority of those voting members present at any
regular or special meeting of the Greenspace Trust shall be the acts of the
Greenspace Trust.
(3)   Regular meetings shall be held at least once quarterly, and special
meetings may be held as specified in the bylaws. All meetings shall be open to
the public in a manner consistent with KRS 61.805—61.810. Full and complete
minutes of all meetings and records of all proceedings, including the number of
votes for and against each motion and the record of the vote of each member,
shall be kept and made available for public inspection.
(4)   The urban county government shall provide an executive director and staff
as needed. The Greenspace Trust staff shall serve as staff to the Greenspace
Trust and shall be responsible for coordinating agendas, preparing minutes and
handling logistical matters in order to expedite the board's function. Within
the limits of the funds appropriated by the council in the annual budget, the
other offices and agencies of the government shall provide the Greenspace
Trust, either directly or by contract or agreement, with the facilities,
materials, supplies, and staff needed for the conduct of its business
(5)   All members of the Greenspace Trust shall be subject to the code of
ethics contained in
article 16 of the Urban County Charter.
(Ord. No. 075-2022 , § 5, 7-7-22)
Sec. 2-340. - Board power and duties.
The powers and duties of the Greenspace Trust include the following:
(1)   Develop a greenspace management plan for the entire urban county,
concentrating on urban service and expansion areas, within twenty-four (24)
months after the first official meeting of the Greenspace Trust. This plan
should be developed for review and adoption by the planning commission as an
amendment to the comprehensive plan. This plan should subsequently be reviewed
and updated every five (5) years concurrent with the comprehensive plan.
(2)   Make specific recommendations to the mayor and council on actions,
including, but not limited to, the following:
(a)   The sale of land or any interest therein held by the urban county
government.
(b)   The acquisition of conservation easements, scenic easements and nature
preserve land.
(c)   The acceptance of property interests acquired by gift.
(3)   Educate citizens about greenspace preservation and maintenance.
(4)   Negotiate the conveyance of property interests.
(5)   Monitor land contained in the greenspace program and conduct annual on-
site inspections. Recommend enforcement of greenspace agreements.
(6)   Hold title to and convey interests in real property.
(7)   Hold title to and convey interest in conservation easements
(8)   Encourage economic development and tourism consistent with the goals of
this article.
(9)   Promote and cooperate development and tourism consistent with the goals
of this article.
(10)   Prepare and present to the mayor and council an annual, written report
which summarizes the previous year's activities.
(11)   Apply for and receive funds from any state, federal or public entity
appropriate to the goals of the trust.
(12)   Solicit and receive contributions and donations from individuals and
groups for the purpose of carrying out its duties as set forth herein.
(13)   Solicit financial and other contributions to the urban county government
or to the Greenspace Trust, including, but not limited to, donations of money,
services and real property.
(14)   Adopt bylaws, rules and regulations as are necessary to carry out its
duties and purposes as set forth in this article.
(Ord. No. 075-2022 , § 6, 7-7-22)
Secs. 2-341—2-344. Reserved.
ARTICLE XXXI. - HOUSING AND SUPPORT SERVICES COMMISSION 17
 
Notes
   Editor's note(s)—Section 1 of Ord. No. 77-91, adopted Apr. 18, 1991, added art.
   XXX, §§ 2-325—2-340, which the editor has redesignated art. XXXI, §§
17 2-345—
   2-350, since Ord. No. 264-90, § 1, adopted Dec. 6, 1990, had previously added
   art. XXX, §§ 2-326—2-334.
Sec. 2-345. - Created.
(a)   A commission is hereby created which shall be known as the "Commission on
Housing and Support Services," hereinafter referred to as "the commission."
(b)   The commission is established for the purpose of providing leadership for
community efforts, in both the public and private sectors, toward the
improvement of housing, support services, education, job training and
employment services for the homeless.
(Ord. No. 77-91, § 1, 4-18-91; Ord. No. 93-93, § 1, 5-20-93)
Sec. 2-346. - Membership.
The commission shall be composed of members of all segments of the local
community, including but not limited to: local government, business, social
service agencies, religious organizations, interested citizens, educators and
the homeless. The commission shall consist of nineteen (19) members, all of
which shall be voting members. The nineteen members shall be appointed by the
mayor subject to confirmation by a majority of the council members, and shall
be representative of the following:
(1)   Non-profit agencies or entities operating in Lexington-Fayette County (8
members);
(2)   General business, banking or mortgage companies or firms operating in
Lexington-Fayette County (5 members);
(3)   State or local government agencies (6 members).
(Ord. No. 77-91, § 1, 4-18-91; Ord. No. 93-93, § 2, 5-20-93; Ord. No. 147-99, §
1, 6-17-99)
Sec. 2-347. - Term.
For all members of the commission created by this article, the term shall be
four (4) years from the date of appointment, provided the terms of those
originally appointed shall be staggered in the following manner: Twelve (12)
members shall be appointed for two (2) years, and seven (7) members shall be
appointed for four (4) years. Vacancies shall be filled for the unexpired term
in the manner prescribed for in the original appointment.
(Ord. No. 77-91, § 1, 4-18-91; Ord. No. 147-99, § 2, 6-17-99)
Sec. 2-348. - Officers.
The commission created by this article shall have a chair appointed by the
mayor to serve for a term of two (2) years and a vice-chair and secretary
elected from the membership as set forth in the bylaws. The officers shall take
office at the first meeting of the commission, and their duties shall be as
implied by their respective titles and as may be specified in the bylaws. The
commission shall determine its own rules and order of business and shall
provide for keeping a record of its proceedings.
(Ord. No. 77-91, § 1, 4-18-91; Ord. No. 93-93, § 3, 5-20-93)
Sec. 2-349. - Quorum.
A majority of the members of the commission created by this article shall
constitute a quorum for the transaction of business at any meeting. The acts of
a majority of the quorum in any regular or special meeting of the commission
shall be the acts of the commission.
(Ord. No. 77-91, § 1, 4-18-91; Ord. No. 93-93, § 4, 5-20-93; Ord. No. 147-99, §
3, 6-17-99)
Sec. 2-350. - Powers and duties.
(a)   General Powers: The commission created by this article may expend such
funds as may become available to it; may examine, report and advise the urban
county government on housing issues; and may form committees and adopt bylaws,
rules and regulations as are necessary to carry out its duties and purposes as
set forth in this article. The commission shall not acquire any interest in any
real property without the prior approval of the mayor and the urban county
council.
(b)   Duties: The commission shall, as permitted by law:
(1)   Oversee implementation of the task force on homelessness recommendations;
(2)   Coordinate community response;
(3)   Establish committees, which may include interested members of the public,
as may be necessary for carrying out its duties set forth herein; and
(4)   Serve as the lead planning agency for the development of the Consolidated
Plan for the United States Department of Housing and Urban Development's
Community Planning and Development Programs.
(5)   Perform any other act necessary or appropriate to carry out the purposes
of this article.
(Ord. No. 77-91, § 1, 4-18-91; Ord. No. 93-93, § 5, 5-20-93; Ord. No. 40-95, §
1, 2-23-95)
Sec. 2-351. - Executive committee.
The provisions of section
2-349 notwithstanding, the commission created by this article may create an
executive committee composed of the chair, the vice-chair, secretary and a
representative of each standing committee chosen by the committee, which shall
have and exercise all of the authority of the commission, subject to the
limitations imposed on the powers of the committees and of the directors of
nonstock, nonprofit corporation by KRS 273.221.
(Ord. No. 93-93, § 6, 5-20-93)
Secs. 2-352—2-360. Reserved.
ARTICLE XXXII. - LEXINGTON-FAYETTE URBAN COUNTY CRIMINAL JUSTICE COMMISSION 18
 
Notes
   Editor's note(s)—Section 1 of Ord. No. 87-91, adopted May 2, 1991, added art.
   XXXI, §§ 2-331—2-336. The editor has redesignated the provisions as art. XXXII,
18 §§
   2-361—2-366, since Ord. No. 77-91 had previously been added as art. XXXI, §§
   2-345—2-350.
Sec. 2-361. - Created.
(a)   A commission is hereby created which shall be known as the Lexington-
Fayette Urban County Criminal Justice Commission, hereinafter referred to as
"the commission."
(b)   The commission is established for the purpose of providing long- and
short-range planning for and coordination of activities among agencies
participating in the criminal justice system.
(Ord. No. 87-91, § 1, 5-2-91)
Sec. 2-362. - Membership.
(a)   The commission shall consist of nineteen (19) ex officio members and two
(2) appointed members. The appointed members shall be appointed by the mayor,
subject to confirmation by a majority of the urban county councilmembers. The
appointed members of the commission shall be selected because of their
demonstrated knowledge or interest in the area of criminal justice.
(b)   The ex officio members shall consist of the commissioner of public
safety, the chief justice of the Fayette circuit court, the chief justice of
the Fayette district court, the commonwealth attorney, the county attorney, the
public defender, the chief of police, the sheriff, the director of detention,
the program administrator for juvenile detention, the commissioner of social
services, the director of comprehensive care, the director of pre-trial
services, the Fayette County circuit clerk, the director of adult probation,
the director of the commonwealth probation and parole office, and the president
of the Fayette County bar association. Additionally, the mayor shall appoint,
subject to confirmation by a majority of the urban county councilmembers, a
member of the Fayette county delegation to the Kentucky General Assembly and an
urban county councilmember. The ex officio members may select a designee
authorized to represent them on the commission. Both the appointed members and
the ex officio members or their designees shall be voting members of the
commission. The office of the mayor and the department of law shall provide
staff and assistance to the commission as needed. Commission members shall
receive no compensation for their services.
(Ord. No. 87-91, § 1, 5-2-91; Ord. No. 173-91, § 1, 7-18-91; Ord. No. 133-93, §
1, 7-8-93; Ord. No. 174-94, § 1, 8-25-94)
Sec. 2-363. - Term.
(a)   The appointed members of the commission shall serve a term of four (4)
years from the date of appointment, provided that the terms of those originally
appointed shall be staggered in the manner required by section
7.02 of the Urban County Charter. Vacancies shall be filled for an unexpired
term in the manner prescribed for the original appointment. Any member may be
appointed for additional terms.
(b)   The ex officio members shall consist of the commissioner of public
safety, the chief justice of the Fayette circuit court, the chief justice of
the Fayette district court, the commonwealth attorney, the county attorney, the
public defender, the chief of police, the sheriff, the director of community
corrections, the program administrator for juvenile detention, the commissioner
of social services, the director of comprehensive care, the director of
pretrial services, the Fayette County circuit clerk, the director of adult
probation, the director of the commonwealth probation and parole office, and
the president of the Fayette County bar association. Additionally, the mayor
shall appoint, subject to confirmation by a majority of the urban county
councilmembers, a member of the Fayette County delegation to the Kentucky
General Assembly and an urban county councilmember. The ex officio members may
select a designee authorized to represent them on the commission. Both the
appointed members and the ex officio members or their designees shall be voting
members of the commission. The office of the mayor and the department of law
shall provide staff and assistance to the commission as needed. Commission
members shall receive no compensation for their services.
(Ord. No. 87-91, § 1, 5-2-91; Ord. No. 333-99, § 4, 12-7-99)
Sec. 2-364. - Officers.
The mayor shall appoint the chairperson and vice-chairperson of the commission,
and the commission shall have any other officers elected from the membership as
the commission deems necessary. The commission shall determine its own rules
and order of business and shall provide for keeping a record of its
proceedings. The board shall meet at least quarterly at a date, place and time
to be selected by the chairperson.
(Ord. No. 87-91, § 1, 5-2-91; Ord. No. 174-94, § 2, 8-25-94)
Sec. 2-365. - Quorum.
A majority of the members of the commission created by this article shall
constitute a quorum for the transaction of business at any meeting. The acts of
a majority of those members present in any regular or special meeting of the
commission shall be the acts of the commission.
(Ord. No. 87-91, § 1, 5-2-91)
Sec. 2-366. - Powers and duties.
The commission created by this article shall, as permitted by law:
(a)   Identify and recommend application for funds from local, state and
federal resources, which can be utilized by the various criminal justice
agencies.
(b)   Gather statistical data and identify trends in the development of the
criminal justice system.
(c)   Coordinate activities of the agencies of the criminal justice agencies
represented on the commission.
(d)   Analyze existing criminal justice policy, develop new policies and make
recommendations to local and state legislative bodies.
(Ord. No. 87-91, § 1, 5-2-91)
Secs. 2-367—2-376. Reserved.

ARTICLE XXXV. - COURT-APPOINTED SPECIAL ADVOCATE BOARD 20
 
Notes
20 Editor's note(s)-Section 1 of Ord. No. 58-94, adopted Apr. 14, 1994, added §§
   2-281-2-386. The editor has designated the provisions art. XXXV.
Sec. 2-381. - Created; purpose.
(1)   A board is hereby created which shall be known as the court-appointed
special advocate board, hereinafter referred to as "board."
(2)   The purpose of the board is to ensure and maintain the high quality of
independent volunteers who represent abused and neglected children in the court
system through the court-appointed special advocate hereinafter referred to as
"CASA," program.
(Ord. No. 58-94, § 1, 4-14-94; Ord. No. 63-2006, § 1, 3-9-06)
Sec. 2-382. - Members.
(1)   The board shall consist of at least sixteen (16) appointed members,
excluding ex officio members. The board, through its bylaws, may provide for a
greater number of appointed members. The appointed members shall be appointed
by the mayor, subject to confirmation by a majority of the urban county council
members. The appointed members of the board shall be selected because of their
demonstrated sincere interest in the purpose of the CASA program and a
commitment to further the program's mission and goals. Appointed members shall
serve a term of four (4) years from the date of appointment, provided that the
terms of those originally appointed shall be staggered in the manner required

7.02 of the Urban County Charter. Vacancies shall be filled for the unexpired

members nor their designees shall be voting members of the board. The division
of police, department of social services and the department of law shall
provide staff and assistance to the board as needed. Board members shall
receive no compensation for their services.

§ 1, 6-23-11)

The board shall, as permitted by law:

federal, public or private organization, as well as solicit and receive
contributions and donations from individuals and groups for the purpose of
carrying out its duties as set forth herein;
(2)   Monitor the CASA program;
(3)   Serve as a communications liaison between the CASA program and the
public;
(4)   Support and promote the CASA program in the areas of legislation;
(5)   Develop community links among other interested professionals;
(6)   Mediate disputes concerning CASA volunteers;
(7)   Establish committees, which may include interested members of the public,
as may be necessary for carrying out the duties as set forth herein; and
(8)   Perform any other act necessary and appropriate to carry out the purposes
of this article.
(Ord. No. 58-94, § 1, 4-14-94; Ord. No. 63-2006, § 3, 3-9-06)
Sec. 2-384. - Officers, records, frequency of meetings.
The mayor shall appoint a chairman pro tem until such time as the bylaws are in
place. He shall take office at the time of the first board meeting. The mayor
shall appoint a paid director and other staff as necessary to assist the board
in carrying out its duties. The board may elect other officers and committees
from the board membership as the board deems necessary. The board shall
determine its own rules and order of business and shall provide for keeping a
record of its proceedings. The board shall meet at least quarterly at a date,
place and time to be selected by the chairman.
(Ord. No. 58-94, § 1, 4-14-94)

A majority of the voting members shall constitute a quorum for transaction of
business at any meeting of the board.
(Ord. No. 58-94, § 1, 4-14-94)
Sec. 2-386. - Contracts, expenditures, bylaws.
The board may enter into contracts; expend funds as may be available to it; and
adopt bylaws, rules and regulations as are necessary to carry out its duties
and purposes as set forth in this article.
(Ord. No. 58-94, § 1, 4-14-94)
ARTICLE XXXVI. - BLUEGRASS CRIMESTOPPERS, INC.
Sec. 2-387. - Creation; purpose; powers.
(a)   The actions of Lana Gibbons, Roger Dalton, Robert Trinler and David
Franklin, all being residents of the county, as incorporators for a nonprofit,
nonstock Kentucky corporation under the provisions of KRS chapter 273, named
"Bluegrass Crimestoppers, Inc.", and hereinafter referred to as "corporation",
and the activities of the corporation, be and are ratified.
(b)   The corporation is organized for the following purposes:
(1)   To foster the detection of crime and encourage persons to report
information about criminal acts;
(2)   To encourage the news and other media to promote the Bluegrass
Crimestoppers and inform the public of its function;
(3)   To assist other crimestoppers organizations in forwarding information
about criminal acts to the appropriate law enforcement agencies; and
(4)   To help law enforcement agencies detect and combat crime by increasing
the flow of information to and between law enforcement agencies.
(c)   The corporation shall possess all the powers conferred upon a corporation
organized under KRS chapter 273 dealing with nonprofit, nonstock corporations
and shall have all powers necessary, proper, convenient or desirable in order
to fulfill and further the purposes of the corporation. The chairperson, the
representative of the division of police, and two (2) members of the board
selected by majority vote of the board shall comprise an executive committee,
which is authorized to act on behalf of the corporation in performing
management and business-related functions.
(Ord. No. 48-96, § 1, 4-4-96)
Sec. 2-388. - Directors.
(a)   The affairs of the corporation are to be conducted by a board of
directors consisting of not less than ten (10) nor more than thirty (30)
individuals. One of the directors shall be a representative of the division of
police. The directors shall be appointed by the mayor subject to confirmation
by a majority of the urban county council members.
(b)   All directors of the corporation shall serve four (4) years from the date
of appointment, provided that the terms shall be staggered in the manner
required by section
7.02 of the Urban County Charter. Vacancies shall be filled for the unexpired
terms in the manner prescribed for the original appointment. Any director may
be reappointed for one (1) additional consecutive term.
(Ord. No. 48-96, § 1, 4-4-96)
Sec. 2-389. - Meetings.
The corporation shall determine its own rules and order of business and shall
provide for keeping a record of its proceedings. The corporation shall meet on
a quarterly basis at a date, place and time to be determined by the board of
directors.
(Ord. No. 48-96, § 1, 4-4-96)
Sec. 2-390. - Quorum.
A majority of the directors shall constitute a quorum for the transaction of
business at any meeting of the board of directors.
(Ord. No. 48-96, § 1, 4-4-96)
ARTICLE XXXVII. - COMMUNITY PARTNERSHIP ACTION COUNCIL
Sec. 2-391. - Created; purpose.
(a)   A council is hereby created which shall be known as the Community
Partnership Action Council, herein referred to as "council".
(b)   The council is established for the purpose of developing strategies for
building a community/police partnership and a community education campaign
focused on crime prevention and facilitating a citizen police academy which
will contribute to the development of stronger ties and ultimately a sense of
partnership between the community and the division of police.
(Ord. No. 51-96, § 1, 4-4-96)
Sec. 2-392. - Members.
(a)   The council shall consist of seventeen (17) appointed members and two (2)
ex officio members. The appointed members shall be appointed by the mayor
subject to confirmation by a majority of the urban county councilmembers. The
mayor shall appoint the following members:
(1)   One (1) member from each council district selected from a list of three
(3) recommendations submitted by each councilmember representing a council
district;
(2)   Three (3) members each of which shall be selected from a list of three
(3) recommendations submitted by each at large councilmember; and
(3)   Two (2) members under the age of eighteen (18).
The appointed members of the council shall have an interest in promoting a
community/police partnership and have a demonstrated ability to constructively
discuss potentially difficult issues and work towards an achievable consensus.
Appointed members shall serve a term of four (4) years from the date of
appointment, provided that the terms of those originally appointed shall be
staggered in the manner required by section
7.02 of the urban county charter. Vacancies shall be filled for an unexpired
term in the manner prescribed for the original appointment. With respect to the
recommendations submitted pursuant to subsection (1) or (2), above, the
Community Action Partnership Council shall notify the appropriate urban county
councilmember that a vacancy exists and request that he or she submit his or
her list of recommendations to the mayor within sixty (60) days. In the event a
list of recommendations is not submitted to the mayor within sixty (60) days of
notification, the mayor may fill the vacancy from a list of recommendations
submitted by the Community Action Partnership Council and its staff, or the
president of the Fayette County Neighborhood Council, so long as the
recommended appointee otherwise meets the membership requirements of this
section.
(b)   The ex officio members shall consist of the urban county government chief
of police and the president of the Fayette County Neighborhood Council. The ex
officio members may select a designee authorized to represent them on the
council.
(c)   Both the appointed members and the ex officio members or their designee
shall be voting members of the council.
(d)   The division of police shall provide staff and assistance to the council
as needed.
(e)   The council shall receive no compensation for their services.
(Ord. No. 51-96, § 1, 4-4-96; Ord. No. 83-2002, § 1, 4-25-02)
Sec. 2-393. - Officers; records; frequency of meetings.
The council may elect officers from the membership as the council deems
necessary. The council shall determine its own rules and order of business and
shall provide for keeping a record of its proceedings. The council shall meet
monthly at a date, place and time to be selected by the council.
(Ord. No. 51-96, § 1, 4-4-96)
Sec. 2-394. - Quorum.
The majority of the members shall constitute a quorum for transaction of
business at any meeting of the council.
(Ord. No. 51-96, § 1, 4-4-96)
Sec. 2-395. - Duties.
The council shall, as permitted by law:
(1)   Develop programs directed at building a community/police partnership;
(2)   Sponsor educational programs focused on crime prevention, such as a
citizen police academy;
(3)   Establish committees, which may include interested members of the public,
as may be necessary for carrying out the duties as set forth herein; and
(4)   Perform any other acts necessary and appropriate to carry out the purpose
of this article.
(Ord. No. 51-96, § 1, 4-4-96)
ARTICLE XXXVIII. - PARKS AND RECREATION ADVISORY BOARD
Sec. 2-396. - Created.
(1)   A board is hereby created which shall be known as the parks and
recreation advisory board of the Lexington-Fayette Urban County Government,
hereinafter sometimes referred to as the "parks board."
(2)   The parks board is established for the purpose of serving as an advisory
board to the division of parks and recreation. In this role, it shall serve as
a vehicle for receiving public opinion and as a vehicle for promoting a
comprehensive parks and recreation delivery system.
(Ord. No. 269-98, § 1, 10-1-98)
Sec. 2-397. - Membership; terms.
(1)   The members of the parks board shall be fifteen (15) in number and shall
be appointed by the mayor, subject to confirmation by a majority of the urban
county councilmembers. Twelve (12) members shall be selected in the following
manner: one (1) member shall reside in each of the twelve (12) council
districts, as those districts exist at the time the appointment is made. Three
(3) members shall be selected in the following manner: one (1) member shall be
a councilmember at large and one (1) member shall be a district councilmember,
recommended by a majority of the urban county councilmembers, and one (1)
member shall be a representative of the Fayette County School System,
recommended by a majority of the Fayette County School Board.
(2)   The members of the parks board shall serve a term of four (4) years from
the date of appointment, provided the terms of those originally appointed shall
be staggered in the following manner: four (4) members shall be appointed for
one (1) year; four (4) members shall be appointed for two (2) years; four (4)
members shall be appointed for three (3) years; and three (3) members shall be
appointed for four (4) years.
(3)   Vacancies shall be filled for an unexpired term in the manner prescribed
for the original appointment. The membership of the appointed councilmembers
shall be terminated upon leaving office as a councilmember.
(4)   No member originally appointed to the parks board who has served one (1)
consecutive full term after his initial term may succeed himself until the
lapse of twelve (12) months from the end of said consecutive term. No later
appointed member who has served two (2) consecutive full terms may succeed
himself until the lapse of twelve (12) months from the end of said consecutive
terms.
(Ord. No. 269-98, § 1, 10-1-98)
Sec. 2-398. - Officers.
The officers of the parks board shall consist of a chairman, a vice-chairman,
and other officers elected from the membership as set forth in the bylaws. They
shall take office at the first meeting of the parks board after election. The
duties of the officers shall be as specified in the bylaws. The parks board
shall determine its own rules and order of business and so provide for keeping
a record of its proceedings.
(Ord. No. 269-98, § 1, 10-1-98)
Sec. 2-399. - Quorum.
A majority of the parks board, that is eight (8) members, shall constitute a
quorum for transaction of business at any meeting of the parks board. The acts
of a majority of those members present at any regular or special meeting of the
parks board shall be the acts of the parks board, provided that it shall take a
vote of ten (10) members to adopt or amend its bylaws.
(Ord. No. 269-98, § 1, 10-1-98)
Sec. 2-400. - Staff.
The director of parks and recreation or his designee shall serve as staff
liaison to the parks board and shall be responsible for coordinating agendas,
preparing minutes and handling logistical matters in order to expedite the
board's function. The members of the parks board should limit contact with the
division of parks and recreation staff to the director or his designee, unless
other contacts are made with his knowledge or approval.
(Ord. No. 269-98, § 1, 10-1-98)
Sec. 2-401. - Powers and duties.
(1)   The parks board shall, as permitted by law:
(a)   Adopt bylaws which are not inconsistent with this article;
(b)   Appoint standing and ad hoc committees, which may be comprised of parks
board members, employees of the urban county government, the public, or any
combination of the foregoing;
(c)   Hold public forums for the purpose of gauging the will of the public on
parks and recreation matters;
(d)   Solicit financial and other contributions to the urban county government,
including donations of real property, for the purposes of parks and recreation
programs;
(e)   Assist the staff of the division of parks and recreation, upon request,
in the performance of their duties in the following areas:
(i)   Interpreting and promoting the division of parks and recreation mission,
goals and objectives to public officials and the general public;
(ii)   Implementing the specifics of a division of parks and recreation public
relations plan;
(iii)   Implementing the specifics of the parks master plan and any other parks
and recreation plans adopted by the government or the division of parks and
recreation;
(iv)   Evaluating current services and facilities of the division of parks and
recreation and divisional priorities;
(v)   Providing the highest standards in division of parks and recreation
leadership, facilities, and services;
(vi)   Reviewing fees and charges and alternate sources of funding to the
division of parks and recreation such as grants, gifts, endowments, etc.; and
(vii)   Providing for a high standard in the preservation, conservation, and
maintenance of all parks, open space, and facilities operated by the division
of parks and recreation.
(f)   Assist the division of parks and recreation in making recommendations to
the mayor and urban county council in the following areas:
(i)   Division of parks and recreation policies and priorities for facilities,
programs, fees, charges, schedules, etc.;
(ii)   Public relation strategies for stimulating public involvement, promoting
services and achieving results;
(iii)   Presentation of the division of parks and recreation budget;
(iv)   Professional development and training of division of parks and
recreation staff;
(v)   Legislation that will promote the mission, goals, and objectives of the
division of parks and recreation;
(vi)   Establishing land acquisition and facility development/improvement
priorities; and
(vii)   Monitoring of services, development of a volunteer program, and
coordination with interest groups in the community.
(g)   Shall prepare and present to the urban county council in work session
written reports on a quarterly basis each calendar year and shall have a place
on the work session agenda, if requested, for the purpose of submission of the
reports.
(2)   The parks board shall not:
(a)   Directly or indirectly operate any parks and recreation program;
(b)   Hold title to any real or personal property;
(c)   Receive or hold any funds;
(d)   Be involved in the selection, supervision, evaluation, or discipline of
urban county government personnel, provided that parks board members may serve
on a selection or recruitment committee;
(e)   Have any direct involvement in the urban county government budget
process, provided that the parks board may assist the director of parks and
recreation in making recommendations as a part of the budget process;
(f)   Expend or commit urban county government funds, provided that the parks
board may authorize expenditure of any funds directly appropriated to it for a
particular purpose by the urban county council;
(g)   Enter into or influence contractual obligations, provided that members of
the parks board may serve as part of a selection team; or
(h)   Represent to the public, media or any other person that they represent
the urban county government or the division of parks and recreation.
(Ord. No. 269-98, § 1, 10-1-98)
Sec. 2-402. - Conflict of interest.
All members of the parks board shall be subject to the code of ethics contained
in
article 16 of the Urban County Charter.
(Ord. No. 269-98, § 1, 10-1-98)
Secs. 2-403—2-420. Reserved.
ARTICLE XXXIX. - TOWN AND GOWN COMMISSION 21
 
Notes
   Editor's note(s)-Section 1 of Ord. No. 289-99, adopted Oct. 21, 1999, added a
21 new §§
   2-396-2-402 to the Code; however, said provisions have been redesignated as §
   2-421-427, at the editor's discretion, for purposes of future expansion.
Sec. 2-421. - Created; purpose.
(a)   A commission is hereby created, which shall be known as the "Town and
Gown Commission," hereinafter referred to as "the commission."
(b)   The commission is established for the purpose of pursuing the
recommendations of the 1999 University of Kentucky Neighborhoods Committee;
improving communication between the University of Kentucky, Transylvania
University, and the Bluegrass Community and Technical College (hereinafter
collectively referred to as the "Universities and College") and other community
elements including neighborhoods, local government, students, business
community and others; and to analyze issues of common concern and develop
recommendations for consideration by the mayor of the urban county government
and the Presidents of the Universities and College.
(Ord. No. 289-99, § 1, 10-21-99; Ord. No. 18-2012, § 1, 2-16-12)
Sec. 2-422. - Membership.
The membership of the commission shall be composed of sixteen (16) appointed
members and eight (8) ex officio members, as follows:
(1)   Eight (8) of the members shall be appointed by the Mayor of the
Lexington-Fayette Urban County Government, subject to confirmation by a
majority of urban county council members, as follows:
a.   One (1) member from the administration of the urban county government;
b.   Three (3) landlord/business community representatives, each of whom own
residential rental property or business concerns in the immediate area of the
main campuses of one (1) of the Universities and College;
c.   Three (3) neighborhood organization representatives, selected from among
nominees to be submitted to the mayor by incorporated neighborhood associations
whose recognized boundaries are contiguous to the border of the main campuses
of one of the Universities and College;
d.   One (1) at large urban county council member.
(2)   The ex officio members shall consist of the urban county council member
from the First District, the urban county council member from the Third
District, the urban county council member from the Eleventh District, the
Executive Director of the Downtown Development Authority, the Lexington-Fayette
Urban County Commissioner of Public Safety, or his or her designee, and the
Student Government Presidents, or their designees, from each of the respective
Universities and College.
(3)   Six (6) of the members shall be appointed by the President of the
University of Kentucky, one (1) of the members shall be appointed by the
President of Transylvania University, and one (1) of the members shall be
appointed by the President of Bluegrass Community Technical College System for
their respective entities, as follows:
a.   Four (4) University of Kentucky administration representatives, one (1)
Transylvania University administration representative, and one (1) Bluegrass
Community Technical College System administration representative; and
b.   Two (2) University of Kentucky student representatives, one (1)
Transylvania University student representative, enrolled at university at the
time of appointment. Discontinuation of enrolled-student status shall
disqualify the incumbent and be cause for a new appointment to be made.
(Ord. No. 289-99, § 1, 10-21-99; Ord. No. 30-2003, § 1, 2-6-03; Ord. No. 18-
2012, § 2, 2-16-12)
Sec. 2-423. - Terms.
Terms of members shall be four (4) years from the date of appointment, provided
the terms of those originally appointed shall be staggered so that five (5)
members shall be appointed for one (1) year, three (3) members shall be
appointed for two (2) years, five (5) members shall be appointed for three (3)
years, and five (5) members shall be appointed for four (4) years. The term
rotation shall be established so that at least one (1) term expires each year
for: LFUCG council/administration; landlord/business community representatives;
university administrators; student representatives; and neighborhood
representatives. Vacancies shall be filled in the same manner as the original
appointment and the successor shall be appointed for the unexpired terms. The
membership of the urban county council members shall be deemed to have been
terminated when their respective term of office on the urban county council
ends, the membership of the Executive Director of the Downtown Development
Authority shall be deemed to have terminated when his or her employment as the
director ends, and the membership of the Lexington-Fayette Urban County
Commissioner of Public Safety shall be deemed to have terminated when his or
her employment as commissioner ends. The first members of the commission shall
assume their duties effective November 1, 1999.
(Ord. No. 289-99, § 1, 10-21-99; Ord. No. 30-2003, § 2, 2-6-03; Ord. No. 18-
2012, § 3, 2-16-12)
Sec. 2-424. - Officers; records.
The commission shall have joint chairpersons to be appointed by the mayor, with
one chairperson selected from those members appointed by the mayor and one
chairperson selected from those members appointed by the President of the
University of Kentucky. The joint chairpersons shall serve for two year terms
and may be appointed for additional terms. A secretary shall be elected from
the membership for a two-year term and the commission shall determine its own
rules and order of business and shall provide for keeping a record of its
proceedings.
(Ord. No. 289-99, § 1, 10-21-99)
Sec. 2-425. - Frequency of meetings.
The commission shall meet at least quarterly at a date, place and time to be
selected by the joint chairpersons, with notice provided in accordance with
applicable open meetings laws.
(Ord. No. 289-99, § 1, 10-21-99)
Sec. 2-426. - Quorum.
A majority of the members of the commission created by this article shall
constitute a quorum for the transaction of business at any meeting. The acts of
a majority of the quorum in any regular or special meeting of the commission
shall be the acts of the commission.
(Ord. No. 289-99, § 1, 10-21-99)
Sec. 2-427. - Powers and duties.
The commission may consider issues of common concern relating to the mutual
health and benefit of the Universities and College and the community, including
but not limited to the condition and availability of affordable housing and its
relationship to the presence of on-campus housing; public transit
opportunities; respective roles of the Universities and College and community
in the regulation of parking, traffic, student behavioral issues, maintenance
and renovation of surrounding properties and infrastructure; matters of common
concern affecting zoning, land use, and the environment; and exploring private/
public development and grant funding opportunities.
(Ord. No. 289-99, § 1, 10-21-99; Ord. No. 18-2012, § 4, 2-16-12)
ARTICLE XL. - DOWNTOWN DEVELOPMENT AUTHORITY
Sec. 2-428. - Created; purpose.
A nonprofit, non-stock corporation shall be created pursuant to Chapter 58 of
the Kentucky Revised Statutes to be known as the "Lexington Downtown
Development Authority, Inc.," hereinafter referred to as the "development
authority." The development authority shall be created to act as an agency,
instrumentality and constituted authority of the urban county government in the
acquisition and financing of any "public project" (as defined in KRS 58.180)
which may be undertaken by the urban county government pursuant to the
provisions of Kentucky law and thus accomplish a public purpose of the urban
county government.
(Ord. No. 312-2001, § 1, 12-13-01)
Sec. 2-429. - Powers and duties.
The development authority shall possess and exercise all powers of a
corporation pursuant to KRS Chapter 58. The development authority may exercise
its powers and duties throughout Fayette County, with particular focus on the
downtown area. The duties of the development authority shall include, but not
be limited to, the following:
(1)   Facilitate development and redevelopment projects within Fayette County;
(2)   Acquire, construct, maintain, add to, and improve any "public project" as
defined in KRS 58.010.
(3)   Coordinate urban county policies and programs relating to public
investment for financing development and redevelopment projects within Fayette
County;
(4)   Develop and coordinate the implementation of downtown, neighborhood,
area-wide and corridor plans and policies of the urban county government,
consistent with, and in coordination with, other urban county departments and
agencies with responsibilities in the same area;
(5)   Establish design and related standards or guidelines for development and
redevelopment projects within Fayette County, consistent with, and in
coordination with, other urban county departments and agencies with
responsibilities in the same area; and
(6)   Coordinate the activities of other urban county government supported
departments, offices, organizations and corporations involved in development
and redevelopment related activities.
Provided, however, the development authority shall not acquire, construct,
maintain, add to, or improve any "public project" as defined in KRS 58.010 with
respect to the Lexington Center Corporation, or its property, without its
consent.
(Ord. No. 312-2001, § 1, 12-13-01)
Sec. 2-430. - Board of directors.
The development authority shall have a board of directors consisting of five
(5) members. The board shall consist of the mayor or the mayor's designee and
such other members as appointed by the mayor, subject to confirmation by a
majority of the urban county council members. The board shall elect one (1) of
its members to act as chairman of the board. The appointed members of the board
shall serve a term of four (4) years from the date of appointment, provided
that the terms of those originally appointed shall be staggered in the manner
required by Section
7.02 of the Urban County Charter. Vacancies shall be filled for the unexpired
term in the manner prescribed for in the original appointment. All members of
the board shall have an interest in downtown redevelopment. Only current board
members shall be permitted to serve as representatives of the development
authority on any other board in which the development authority has a
participatory role.
(Ord. No. 312-2001, § 1, 12-13-01; Ord. No. 153-2017 , § 2, 10-12-17)
Sec. 2-431. - Officers; records; frequency of meetings.
The development authority is authorized to employ an executive director or any
other personnel as needed or may contract with another entity for these
services. The board of directors may elect other officers as the board deems
necessary. The duties of the officers shall be as specified in the bylaws. The
board shall determine its own rules and order of business and shall provide for
keeping a record of its proceedings. The board shall meet at least quarterly at
a date, place and time to be selected by the chairman.
(Ord. No. 312-2001, § 1, 12-13-01; Ord. No. 153-2017 , § 4, 10-12-17)
Sec. 2-432. - Quorum.
A majority of the board of directors shall constitute a quorum for transaction
of business at any meeting of the development authority. The acts of the
majority of those members present at any regular or special meeting of the
development authority shall be the acts of the development authority.
(Ord. No. 312-2001, § 1, 12-13-01)
Sec. 2-433. - Bylaws.
The board of directors may adopt bylaws, rules and regulations as are necessary
to carry out its duties and purposes as set forth in this article.
(Ord. No. 312-2001, § 1, 12-13-01)
Secs. 2-434—2-440. Reserved.
ARTICLE XLI. - INTERNAL AUDIT BOARD 22
 
Notes
   Editor's note(s)-Ord. No. 63-2002, §§
   1-9, adopted March 21, 2002, enacted provisions which were intended for
22 codification as Ch. 2, Art. XL, §§
   2-428-2-436. As those section numbers are already in use, these new
   provisions have been included herein as Art. XLI, §§
   2-441-2-449.
Sec. 2-441. - Established.
A board is hereby established which shall be known as the internal audit board.
(Ord. No. 63-2002, § 1, 3-21-02)
Sec. 2-442. - Members.
(a)   The internal audit board shall consist of seven (7) voting members
appointed by the mayor and two (2) ex-officio, non-voting members appointed as
follows:
(1)   Four (4) members shall be audit, accounting or legal professionals from
the community at large, with CIA, CMA, CPA or other appropriate professional
certifications, two (2) of whom shall be based upon a recommendation made by
the majority of the urban county council, appointed by the mayor and approved
by majority vote of the urban county council;
(2)   Two (2) members shall be selected from the membership of the urban county
council, approved by a majority of the urban county council;
(3)   One (1) member shall be the mayor or his designee; and
(4)   The council administrator and the chief administrative officer shall
serve as ex-officio, non-voting members of the board.
(b)   The members of the board shall serve without compensation but shall be
reimbursed for expenses necessarily incurred in the performance of their
duties.
(c)   A board member may be removed from office by the urban county council
after a hearing by a vote of two-thirds ( 2/3 ) of the members of the council
and only for neglect of duty, malfeasance, conflict of interest or misconduct.
The hearing shall be initiated by the vice-mayor, who shall prepare a written
statement setting forth the reasons for removal. The hearing shall be chaired
by the mayor. The member to be removed shall be notified of the proposed
removal and the reason therefore by registered mail sent to the member's last
known address at least ten (10) days prior to the hearing. The member to be
removed may employ counsel for representation. A record of the hearing shall be
made.
(Ord. No. 63-2002, § 2, 3-21-02; Ord. No. 61-2011, § 1, 5-12-11)
Sec. 2-443. - Terms.
All board members, with the exception of the ex-officio members, shall serve
four (4) years from the date of appointment, provided that the terms shall be
staggered in the manner required by section
7.02 of the Urban County Charter. The ex-officio members shall serve only so
long as they hold the position of council administrator or chief administrative
officer. The membership of the mayor or his designee and urban county council
members shall be deemed to have been terminated when their respective term of
office as mayor or on the urban county council ends. Vacancies shall be filled
for any unexpired term in the manner prescribed for the original appointment.
Any board member may be reappointed for two (2) additional full terms.
(Ord. No. 63-2002, § 3, 3-21-02; Ord. No. 61-2011, § 2, 5-12-11)
Sec. 2-444. - Officers.
The officers of the board shall consist of a chairman and a vice-chairman
chosen from the members from the community at large and elected annually by
majority vote of the voting members of the board. The chairman may not serve
more than two (2) consecutive one-year terms.
(Ord. No. 63-2002, § 4, 3-21-02; Ord. No. 61-2011, § 3, 5-12-11)
Sec. 2-445. - Quorum.
A majority of the voting members of the board shall constitute a quorum for the
transaction of business at any meeting of the board.
(Ord. No. 63-2002, § 5, 3-21-02)
Sec. 2-446. - Meetings.
Regular meetings shall be held at least quarterly, and special meetings may be
held as specified in KRS 61.823. All meetings shall be open to the public in a
manner consistent with KRS 61.805—61.850. Full and complete minutes of all
meetings and records of all proceedings, including the number of votes for and
against each motion and the record of the vote of each member, shall be kept
and made available for public inspection.
(Ord. No. 63-2002, § 6, 3-21-02)
Sec. 2-447. - Bylaws.
The board shall adopt bylaws, rules and order of business, which shall be
approved by the urban county council. The board shall provide for keeping a
record of its proceedings.
(Ord. No. 63-2002, § 7, 3-21-02; Ord. No. 61-2011, § 4, 5-12-11)
Sec. 2-448. - Staff.
The urban county government shall provide staff as needed.
(Ord. No. 63-2002, § 8, 3-21-02)
Sec. 2-449. - Powers and duties.
(a)   The powers and duties of the board include the following:
(1)   To supervise, coordinate, evaluate, monitor, and implement the internal
audit function of the urban county government;
(2)   To ensure compliance with all federal, state, and local laws relating to
financial matters; and
(3)   To cooperate with the external auditor in order to reduce as much as
possible, the cost to the urban county government of having an external audit
performed.
(b)   The priorities of the powers and duties contained in subsection (1) above
shall be determined by the board.
(Ord. No. 63-2002, § 9, 3-21-02)
Sec. 2-450. - Reserved.
ARTICLE XLII. - ARTS COMMISSION 23
 
Notes
   Editor's note(s)-Ord. No. 203-2002, § 1, adopted July 16, 2002, enacted
   provisions intended for use as §§
23 2-443-2-447. As those sections are already in use, these new provisions have
   been renumbered §§
   2-451-2-455, as set forth herein.
Sec. 2-451. - Creation; purpose.
(a)   A commission is hereby created which shall be known as the Lexington-
Fayette Urban County Government Public Arts Commission, hereinafter referred to
as the "commission".
(b)   The commission is established for the following purposes:
(1)   Advising the mayor and the urban county council on the selection,
acquisition, funding, placement, maintenance, and conservation of public art,
public art events, and public monuments by the urban county government,
consistent with the Public Art Master Plan; and
(2)   Reviewing applications for installation of permanent visual artwork in
public spaces from external sources, including, but not limited to, memorials,
monuments and lighting projects, for its aesthetic opportunities with regard to
its design and installation, and toward the conservation of permanent artwork.
(Ord. No. 203-2002, § 1, 7-16-02; Ord. No. 233-2002, § 1, 9-12-02; Ord. No.
057-2022 , § 1, 6-23-22)
Sec. 2-451.1. - Definitions.
(a)   Artist means a practitioner of the arts whose objective is to create
original works of art and is generally recognized as accomplished by others in
his or her field.
(b)   Permanent artwork means visual artwork including, but not limited to, a
fresco, mosaic, sculpture, and other architectural embellishment of functional
art created by a professional artist, artisan or craftsperson; and any work of
visual art including, but not limited to, a drawing, painting, sculpture,
mosaic, photograph, work of calligraphy or work of graphic art or mixed media.
All such artwork that is designed to remain in place for one (1) year or longer
is defined as permanent. All such permanent artwork described herein shall
become the property of the Urban County Government upon placement.
(c)   Public spaces means any real property or improvements owned or leased by
the Lexington-Fayette Urban County Government and open to the public including,
but not limited to: courthouses, administrative office buildings, plazas,
rights-of-way and parks.
(Ord. No. 057-2022 , § 2, 6-23-22)
Sec. 2-452. - Membership.
(a)   The commission shall consist of sixteen (16) appointed members.
(b)   The appointed members shall be residents of Fayette County and shall have
demonstrated an interest in the arts and the effect of same on communities and
individual lives. They shall be appointed by the mayor, subject to confirmation
by the urban county council, from the following:
(1)   Two (2) architects or design professionals;
(2)   Three (3) professional artists, with at least one (1) possessing public
art experience;
(3)   Two (2) arts administration professionals;
(4)   One (1) representative of the Lexington-Fayette County business
community;
(5)   One (1) representative of the Lexington-Fayette Urban County Government;
(6)   One (1) representative from the community at large;
(7)   One (1) representative from the Lexington Convention and Visitors Bureau;
(8)   One (1) member of the Lexington-Fayette Urban County Council;
(9)   One (1) representative from the Office of the Urban County Mayor;
(10)   One (1) licensed civil engineer;
(11)   One (1) landscape architect; and
(12)   A representative from LexArts, who shall be a non-voting, ex officio
member.
(Ord. No. 203-2002, § 1, 7-16-02; Ord. No. 54-2018 , § 1, 8-30-18; Ord. No. 24-
2019 , § 1, 4-11-19; Ord. No. 057-2022 , § 3, 6-23-22)
Sec. 2-453. - Terms.
(a)   Members of the commission shall serve a term of four (4) years from the
date of appointment, provided the terms of those originally appointed shall be
staggered in the following manner:
Two (2) members shall be appointed for one (1) year;
Three (3) members shall be appointed for two (2) years;
Three (3) members shall be appointed for three (3) years; and
Three (3) members shall be appointed for four (4) years.
(b)   Vacancies in the membership shall be filled for an unexpired term in the
manner prescribed for the original appointment.
(c)   No member who has served two (2) consecutive four-year terms may succeed
himself until the lapse of twelve (12) months from the end of said consecutive
terms.
(d)   A member of the commission shall be removed only by a majority vote of
the urban county council, and only for cause.
(Ord. No. 203-2002, § 1, 7-16-02; Ord. No. 72-2018 , § 1, 10-11-18; Ord. No.
24-2019 , § 2, 4-11-19)
Sec. 2-454. - Officers; rules; quorum; meetings.
(a)   The officers of the commission shall consist of a chair and a vice-chair,
and other officers elected from the membership as set forth in the bylaws. They
shall take office at the first meeting of the commission after their election.
The duties of the officers shall be as specified in the bylaws. The commission
shall determine its own rules and order of business and so provide for keeping
a record of its proceedings.
(b)   A majority of the voting members of the commission shall constitute a
quorum for transaction of business at any meeting of the commission. The acts
of a majority of those voting members present at any regular or special meeting
of the commission shall constitute the acts of the commission.
(c)   The commission shall meet at a minimum on a quarterly basis at a date,
place and time to be determined by the commission. All meetings shall be open
to the public in a manner consistent with the Kentucky Open Meetings Act.
(d)   Special meetings may be called by the chair of the commission or when a
majority of the members of the commission requests a special meeting. At least
twenty-four (24) hours notice of any special meeting shall be given. All
special meetings shall be open meetings held and noticed in compliance with the
Kentucky Open Meetings Act.
(e)   The day-to-day responsibilities of running the business of the commission
will be undertaken by a staff person in the office of the mayor.
(Ord. No. 203-2002, § 1, 7-16-02; Ord. No. 54-2018 , § 2, 8-30-18; Ord. No. 24-
2019 , § 3, 4-11-19; Ord. No. 057-2022 , § 4, 6-23-22)
Sec. 2-455. - Duties.
The commission shall, as permitted by law:
(1)   Adopt bylaws which are not inconsistent with this article;
(2)   Make recommendations to the mayor and the urban county council on the
development, selection, acquisition, funding, placement, maintenance and
conservation of public art and public art events by the urban county
government, consistent with the Public Art Master Plan, including the use of
the Percent for Art Fund;
(3)   Review applications and proposals for permanent artwork in public spaces
pursuant to criteria identified herein;
(4)   Advise the department of general services, division of risk management,
other appropriate urban county government divisions, and the councilmember in
whose district artwork is proposed to be placed at the time a proposal is
received. Further, any work of art requiring extraordinary operation or
maintenance expenses shall receive approval prior to placement and installation
from the commissioner of the department of general services;
(5)   Promulgate rules and regulations consistent with the Public Art Master
Plan and this article that are approved by the Urban County Council, including,
but not limited to, 1) a selection process and selection criteria for the
approval of artwork for public spaces from applications by external sources,
and 2) the process and criteria for making recommendations for the acquisition,
funding, and placement of public art by the urban county government from the
commission, to facilitate the implementation of its responsibilities hereunder;
(6)   Ensure that the interaction of the artwork and the function of the public
space will be compatible;
(7)   Recommend purchase of works of art or commission of the design;
(8)   Make recommendations regarding the design, execution and/or placement of
works of art; and
(9)   Provide information and make recommendations on operation or maintenance
expenses associated with particular art or a particular location and the
interaction of art work with the function of its location, and provide for such
artwork and installation that will not impede such function.
(Ord. No. 203-2002, § 1, 7-16-02; Ord. No. 057-2022 , § 5, 6-23-22)
Sec. 2-455.1. - Code of ethics.
All members of the commission shall be subject to the Code of Ethics contained
in
Article 16 of the Urban County Charter, and agree to comply with all safety and
loss policies of the Urban County Government.
(Ord. No. 057-2022 , § 5, 6-23-22)
Sec. 2-456. - Commission authorized to proceed.
The commission shall be appointed and authorized to proceed upon the adoption
by the urban county council of an ordinance or resolution approving the funding
mechanism for the public art program.
(Ord. No. 314-2002, § 1, 12-5-02)
ARTICLE XLIII. - ACCESS LEXINGTON COMMISSION 24
 
Notes
   Ord. No. 012-2023 , §§
24 2-5, adopted February 9, 2023, renamed art. XLIII from "Commission for
   People with Disabilities" to "Access Lexington Commission."
Sec. 2-457. - Created.
A commission is hereby created which shall be known as the "Access Lexington
Commission."
(Ord. No. 364-2006, § 1, 12-7-06; Ord. No. 23-2016, § 1, 2-18-16 ; Ord. No.
012-2023 , § 2, 2-9-23)
Sec. 2-458. - Membership.
(a)   The commission shall consist of nineteen (19) members, which shall be
appointed by the mayor, subject to confirmation by the council.
(b)   The nineteen (19) members shall be representatives of the following:
(1)   Two (2) ex-officio members from the Lexington-Fayette Urban County
Council;
(2)   Four (4) members from organizations or individuals representing people
with specific disabilities;
(3)   One (1) member representing the business community;
(4)   One (1) member representing a regional college or university;
(5)   One (1) member representing rehabilitation professionals;
(6)   One (1) member representing a public transportation agency;
(7)   Two (2) members from employment and/or education advocacy organizations;
(8)   Two (2) members from the community at large;
(9)   One (1) ex-officio member shall be the ADA coordinator for LFUCG, or
their designee;
(10)   One (1) ex-officio member shall be the director of building inspection,
or their designee;
(11)   One (1) ex-officio member shall be the commissioner of social services,
or their designee;
(12)   One (1) ex-officio member shall be the commissioner of public safety, or
their designee; and
(13)   One (1) ex-officio member shall be either the commissioner of
environmental quality and public works or the director of the division of
planning, or their designee.
(Ord. No. 364-2006, § 1, 12-7-06; Ord. No. 151-2012, § 1, 11-29-12; Ord. No.
130-2014, § 1, 10-9-14; Ord. No. 012-2023 , § 3, 2-9-23)
Sec. 2-459. - Term.
The members of the commission, other than ex-officio members, shall serve a
term of four (4) years from the date of appointment, provided the terms of
those originally appointed shall be staggered as provided in Section
7.02 of the Charter. Vacancies shall be filled for the unexpired term in the
manner prescribed for the original appointment. Any member may be reappointed
for additional terms. The membership of the ex-officio members shall be deemed
to have terminated upon their leaving office or employment.
(Ord. No. 364-2006, § 1, 12-7-06; Ord. No. 012-2023 , § 4, 2-9-23)
Sec. 2-460. - Officers.
The commission shall have a chairperson and a vice-chairperson elected by its
membership to serve for terms of two (2) years. They shall take office at the
first meeting of the commission. The vice-chairperson shall preside in the
absence of the chairperson. The commission shall determine its own rules and
order of business and shall provide for keeping record of its proceedings.
(Ord. No. 364-2006, § 1, 12-7-06; Ord. No. 130-2014, § 2, 10-9-14; Ord. No. 91-
2019 , § 1, 11-14-19)
Sec. 2-461. - Quorum.
A majority of the commission shall constitute a quorum for transaction of
business at any meeting of the commission. The acts of a majority of those
members present at any regular or special meeting of the commission shall be
the acts of the commission.
(Ord. No. 364-2006, § 1, 12-7-06)
Sec. 2-462. - Meetings.
The commission shall meet in regular public session at least six (6) times a
year, at a time and place designated by it. Special meetings may be called by
the chairperson or a majority of the members of the commission.
(Ord. No. 364-2006, § 1, 12-7-06; Ord. No. 130-2014, § 3, 10-9-14)
Sec. 2-463. - Duties and functions of the commission.
The commission shall:
(a)   Advise the mayor and the council on issues of access, representation,
employment, housing and quality of life affecting people with disabilities and
their families.
(b)   Serve as a resource for people with disabilities and their families to
express concerns and solutions regarding issues affecting them.
(c)   Publicize the role of the commission for people with disabilities and the
resources available to assist people with disabilities, employers, housing
representatives, business owners, engineers and architects, and others who have
a role in bettering the life of Lexington-Fayette County residents.
(d)   Promote awareness to the general public of the capabilities, needs and
desires of people with disabilities.
(e)   Publicly recognize the efforts of employers, businesses, schools,
organizations, individuals, and others who have demonstrated outstanding
support of programs and services for people with disabilities.
(f)   Serve as advocate for accessibility issues and implementation of plans
and projects to improve services for people with disabilities.
(g)   Advise urban county departments and divisions on policy matters which
affect the daily lives of people with disabilities, especially with regard to
public facilities.
(Ord. No. 364-2006, § 1, 12-7-06; Ord. No. 23-2016, § 2, 2-18-16 ; Ord. No.
012-2023 , § 5, 2-9-23)
ARTICLE XLIV. - CORRIDORS COMMISSION
Sec. 2-464. - Created and purpose.
A commission is hereby created which shall be known as the "corridors
commission." It shall be the purpose of the corridors commission to assess the
major roads of Lexington-Fayette County, especially the major and minor
arterials, regarding but not limited to aesthetic qualities, viewsheds,
landscaping, fencing, signage, litter control, bike and pedestrian
considerations and other elements the commission may deem appropriate.
(Ord. No. 137-2009, § 1, 7-2-09; Ord. No. 40-2015, § 1, 4-30-15 )
Sec. 2-465. - Membership.
   The Commission shall consist of thirteen (13) voting members. Of these
members, one (1) member shall be a district councilmember representing either
the first, second or sixth district; one (1) member shall be a district
councilmember representing either the fourth, seventh or eighth district; one
(1) member shall be a district councilmember representing either the ninth,
tenth or twelfth district; one (1) member shall be a district councilmember
representing either the third, fifth or eleventh district; one (1) member shall
be an at-large councilmember; three (3) members shall be from the community at-
large; one (1) of the community at-large members shall be a representative of
the Fayette County Neighborhood Council; one (1) member shall be a
representative of the Tree Board; one (1) member shall be a representative of
the Lexington Council Garden Clubs; one (1) member shall be a representative of
District Seven of the Kentucky Transportation Cabinet; one (1) member shall be
representative of Bluegrass Greensource; one (1) member shall be a
representative from the utility industry. There shall be seven (7) members in a
non-voting capacity: one (1) member representing alternative modes of
transportation; one (1) member representing the MPO staff; the urban forester;
one (1) member shall be a representative of District Seven of the Kentucky
Transportation Cabinet; one (1) member shall be from the office of the
Commissioner of General Services or a senior designee; one (1) member shall be
from the office of the Commissioner of Environmental Quality and Public Works
or a senior designee; and one (1) member representing the Complete Streets
Manager. The members shall be appointed by the Mayor subject to confirmation by
the Urban County Council. The members of the Commission shall serve without
compensation but shall be reimbursed for expenses necessarily incurred in the
performance of their duties.
(Ord. No. 137-2009, § 1, 7-2-09; Ord. No. 145-2012, § 1, 11-15-12; Ord. No. 40-
2014, § 1, 4-24-14; Ord. No. 153-2014, § 1, 12-4-14; Ord. No. 68-2019 , § 1, 9-
12-19; Ord. No. 020-2025, § 1, 3-20-25)
Sec. 2-466. - Term.
All commission members shall serve four (4) years from the date of appointment
provided that the terms shall be staggered in the manner required by section
7.02 of the Urban County Charter. Vacancies shall be filled for an unexpired
term in the manner prescribed for the original appointment. Any commission
member may be reappointed for an additional term. No commission member shall
serve more than two (2) consecutive full terms, and can be reappointed after a
lapse of twelve (12) months from the end of the second consecutive full term.
(Ord. No. 137-2009, § 1, 7-2-09)
Sec. 2-467. - Officers.
The officers of the commission shall consist of a chairperson who shall be a
councilmember appointed by the mayor and a vice-chairperson who shall be a
councilmember appointed by the chairperson.
(Ord. No. 137-2009, § 1, 7-2-09)
Sec. 2-468. - Quorum.
A majority of the voting appointed members of the commission shall constitute a
quorum for the transaction of business at any meeting of the commission.
(Ord. No. 137-2009, § 1, 7-2-09; Ord. No. 230-2009, § 1, 11-5-09)
Sec. 2-469. - Meetings.
Regular meetings shall be held at least once quarterly and special meetings may
be held as specified in the by-laws. All meetings shall be open to the public
in the manner consistent with KRS 61.805 through 61.810. Full and complete
minutes of all meetings and records of all proceedings, including number of
votes for and against each motion and the record of the vote of each member,
shall be kept and made available for public inspection.
(Ord. No. 137-2009, § 1, 7-2-09)
Sec. 2-470. - By-laws.
The commission shall adopt its own by-laws, rules and order of business and
shall provide for keeping a record of its proceedings.
(Ord. No. 137-2009, § 1, 7-2-09)
Sec. 2-471. - Staff.
The Urban County Government shall provide staff as needed.
(Ord. No. 137-2009, § 1, 7-2-09)
Sec. 2-472. - Powers and duties.
The powers and duties of the commission include the following:
Any waivers that the corridors committee (now corridors commission) is
authorized to grant by separate ordinance and resolution shall also require
approval of the council.
Review and assess the corridors along major roads, major and minor arterials in
Lexington-Fayette County regarding but not limited to aesthetic qualities,
landscaping, fencing, signage, litter control, bike and pedestrian
considerations and other elements the commission may deem appropriate.
Make specific recommendations to the mayor and council on issues before the
commission.
(Ord. No. 137-2009, § 1, 7-2-09)
ARTICLE XLV. - AFFORDABLE HOUSING GOVERNING BOARD
Sec. 2-473. - [Created.]
A board is hereby created which shall be known as the "Affordable Housing
Governing Board".
(Ord. No. 101-2014, § 1, 9-11-14)
Sec. 2-474. - [Members.]
The Board shall consist of thirteen (13) members, which shall be appointed by
the mayor subject to confirmation by the council. The thirteen (13) members
shall consist of two (2) members from the Lexington-Fayette Urban County
Council; each of the remaining members shall have extensive experience in one
or more of the following areas: homelessness and emergency housing; social and
support services; affordable housing management; grants administration and/or
philanthropic giving; housing construction; commercial or mixed-use
development; property leasing or rental housing; real estate management;
financial management, capital markets, or affordable housing financing.
Additionally, to the extent possible, the composition of the Board shall be
representative of the social, economic, cultural, ethnic and racial groups
which compose the population of Lexington-Fayette County.
(Ord. No. 101-2014, § 1, 9-11-14)
Sec. 2-475. - [Terms.]
For all appointed members of the Board, the term shall be four (4) years from
the date of appointment, provided the terms of those originally appointed shall
be staggered in the following manner: six (6) members shall be appointed for
four (4) years and five (5) members shall be appointed for two (2) years.
Vacancies shall be filled for the unexpired term in the manner prescribed for
the original appointment. No member may serve more than two (2) consecutive
four (4) year terms. The membership of the Urban County Council member shall be
deemed to have terminated upon his/her leaving office as a member of the Urban
County Council.
(Ord. No. 101-2014, § 1, 9-11-14)
