DIVISION 1. - ORDINANCE NUMBER 3590 AND AMENDMENTS
Sec. 6-47. - Definitions.
The following words and phrases as used in this division, unless a different
meaning is plainly required by the context, shall have the following meanings:
(1)   Employee shall mean all employees of the urban county government who were
included in the classified service of the City of Lexington on December 31,
1973, and who chose to stay under the pension system created by Ordinance No.
3590, as amended.
(2)   Member shall mean any person included in the membership of the retirement
system as provided in section
6-50.
(3)   Board shall mean the board of trustees of the pension fund provided in
section
6-49.
(4)   Pension fund shall mean the moneys derived from the employees and the
levy of a special tax, either or both, or any sum derived from any other
source, a gift or otherwise, to be used for the retirement of employees after
the prescribed number of years of service and for the benefit of disabled
employees, and for the benefit of widows and dependent children and parents in
the case of the death of an employee within the scope of his employment
according to the terms of this division.
(5)   Prior service shall mean service rendered prior to the first day of
February, 1939, for which credit is allowable under the provisions of section
6-51.
(6)   Widow shall mean, for members who sever employment on or after December
1, 1973, a person legally married to a member (whether male or female) where
there has been no decree of divorce entered dissolving such marriage and such
marriage is in full force and effect at the time of death of the member and
where there has been no decree of divorce from bed or board secured by the
member and where such member's spouse has not at the time of death of such
member voluntarily abandoned such member. For severances of employment on or
after December 1, 1973, the term "widow" shall also mean widowers.
(7)   Invalid dependent (husband) shall mean a man legally married to a member
where there has been no divorce at the time of the death of the member and
where they are not legally separated and where the husband has not voluntarily
abandoned his wife and is wholly dependent upon her for his support.
(8)   Monthly salary shall mean the monthly salary actually received by the
employee exclusive of compensation for overtime.
(9)   Average monthly salary shall mean the monthly salary actually received by
the employee based over a period of the three (3) highest years' salary
received by the employee, and shall not include compensation paid for overtime
work.
(10)   Year means full and partial years computed on the basis of one-twelfth
year for each month of service in which the employee made a contribution to the
pension fund.
(Ord. No. 3590, § 1, 1-3-57; Ord. No. 4030, § 1, 3-17-60; Ord. No. 305-73, §§
1, 8, 12-27-73; Ord. No. 204-76, § 1, 10-26-76)
Sec. 6-48. - Management and operation of system.
The retirement system for employees of the urban county government as
established in 1939 shall continue to operate under the management of the board
of trustees of the pension fund for the purpose of providing disability and
retirement allowances and death benefits for members of such retirement system.
(Ord. No. 3590, § 2, 1-3-57)
Sec. 6-49. - Board of trustees; members, officers; investment of funds.
(a)   The membership of the board of trustees of the pension fund shall consist
of the mayor, the commissioner of finance, the director of human resources,
four (4) council members subject to confirmation by a majority of the council
members, and three (3) retired members who shall be elected from the retirees
of the fund. Members elected to the board of trustees shall hold their offices
for a period of two (2) years and/or until their successors have been elected
and qualified. The mayor shall be chairman of the board. In addition thereto,
but without having a vote on any question that comes before the board, the
council clerk shall be ex officio secretary of the board. The commissioner of
finance shall be ex officio treasurer of the board.
(1)   Retiree board members—Regular elections. Beginning in December, 1992, and
continuing every second year thereafter, an election shall be held by the
retired members of the pension fund. This election shall be conducted by mail
ballot of the retired members. For all retired member elections conducted after
December 1, 2022, the council clerk shall send written notification of the
upcoming election to all retired members no later than October 1, and shall
seek nominations for a retired member to serve on the board. Nominations for
candidates for retiree positions on the board shall be submitted to the council
clerk no later than November 1, and shall be supported by either one (1)
signature of a retired member of the fund nominating another member or by a
signed self-nomination of a retired member. The council clerk, no later than
November 1, shall inquire of each nominee who did not self-nominate to verify
that the person consents to participation as a candidate in the election. The
council clerk shall not include on the ballot any candidate who did not self-
nominate if such candidate informs the council clerk that he or she does not
wish to be included on the ballot. The council clerk shall make a written
record documenting any such refusal and maintain it with records relating to
the subject election. Secret mail ballots shall be mailed to all retiree
members no later than November 25, and returned no later than December 1. The
council clerk and commissioner of finance shall verify membership, open and
count the mail ballots, and then prepare a report to the board of trustees for
approval at a regularly scheduled meeting of the board of trustees, and every
second year thereafter. After the election deadline has passed, if a successful
candidate is unable or unwilling to serve for any reason, the candidate who
received the next highest number of votes shall be declared the winner of such
board position.
(2)   Retiree board members—Special elections. The board of trustees shall hold
a special election to fill the unexpired term of any retiree position on the
board of trustees. The nomination, voting and validation of election results
procedures for a special election shall be identical to the procedures for
regular elections except that a special election may be initiated in any
calendar month as necessary.
(3)   Retiree board members—Vacancies unfilled by election. Notwithstanding the
foregoing, if one (1) or more of the three (3) retired board of trustee
positions cannot be filled due to an insufficient number of retired members
being willing or able to serve, any such vacancy shall be filled by the mayor
with council approval as authorized by KRS 67A.320. Not later than six (6)
months prior to the expiration of a term of a retiree board member that is
anticipated to be unfilled by election, the clerk shall give written notice, if
practicable, to non-retiree beneficiaries of the fund of the pending board
vacancy and determine if any non-retiree beneficiary is interested in
consideration for appointment to the retiree position. No later than two (2)
months prior to the expiration of a term of a retiree board member that is
anticipated to be unfilled by election, the board shall forward to the office
of the mayor the names of any non-retiree beneficiaries of the retirement fund
who are interested in appointment to a retiree position on the board for
consideration for an appointment. In the event of any retiree member vacancy
unfilled by election, the mayor shall appoint a non-retiree beneficiary to fill
the vacancy on the board, subject to council approval. In the event of any
retiree member vacancy that is unfilled by election, and where there are an
insufficient number of non-retiree beneficiaries willing or able to serve, any
such vacancy shall be filled by appointment by the mayor subject to the
approval of the council as authorized by KRS 67A.320.
(b)   Such board shall have exclusive control and management of the pension
fund.
(c)   The board of trustees shall have power to make all needful rules and
regulations for its government in the discharge of its duties and shall hear
and decide all applications for relief and pension on retirement allowances
under this division; and the decision of the board of trustees on any such
application shall be final and conclusive, and not subject to revision or
reversal, except by such board; and a record shall be kept of all the meetings
and proceedings of such board.
(d)   The board of trustees shall have the power to draw such pension funds
from the treasurer and invest the same or any part thereof in the name of the
board of trustees of the city employees' pension fund in interest-bearing bonds
of the United States, State of Kentucky, or any county or city of the first,
second or third class of the State of Kentucky, or in any securities in which
trustees or guardians are permitted to invest trust or guardianship funds under
the laws of the state.
(Ord. No. 3590, § 3, 1-3-57; Ord. No. 5313, § 1, 9-23-65; Ord. No. 5519, § 1,
4-14-66; Ord. No. 63-72, § 1, 4-13-72; Ord. No. 205-72, § 1, 9-28-72; Ord. No.
305-73, § 9, 12-27-73; Ord. No. 102-85, § 3, 5-30-85; Ord. No. 45-89, § 1, 3-7-
89; Ord. No. 90-92, § 1, 6-25-92; Ord. No. 197-92, § 1, 10-29-92; Ord. No. 29-
2002, § 1, 2-13-02; Ord. No. 99-2017 , § 1, 6-15-17; Ord. No. 088-2022 , § 1,
8-30-22)
Sec. 6-49.1. - Civil service employees on employees pension fund board.
The three (3) civil service employees to be elected to the employees pension
fund board shall consist of one (1) from the department of sanitation and
public works, street and roads, and sewer divisions; one (1) from the
department of sanitation and public works, division of solid waste; and one (1)
from other departments of the merged government.
(Ord. No. 26-74, § 1, 3-7-74)
Charter references(s)—Pension fund boards, §
7.04.
Sec. 6-50. - Membership in retirement plan.
Membership in the retirement plan shall mean all employees of the urban county
government who were included in the classified service of the City of Lexington
on December 31, 1973, and who chose to stay under the pension system created by
Ordinance No. 3590 as amended.
(Ord. No. 3590, § 4, 1-3-57)
Sec. 6-51. - Prior service; prior service certificates.
Under such rules and regulations as the board shall adopt, each member of the
retirement system who was an employee at any time during the year 1938 and who
became a member during the year 1939 shall file a detailed statement of all
services as an employee rendered by him prior to February 1, 1939, for which he
claims credit and of such other facts as the board may require for the proper
operation of the retirement system.
The board shall not allow credit as service for any period of more than one (1)
month's duration during which the employee was absent without pay.
Subject to the above restrictions and as to such other rules and regulations as
the board may adopt, the board shall verify, as soon as practicable after the
filing of such statements of service, the service therein claimed.
Upon verification of the statement of service, the board shall issue prior
service certificates certifying to such member the length of prior service with
which he is credited. So long as membership continues, a prior service
certificate shall be final and conclusive for retirement purposes as to such
services; however, within one (1) year from the date of the issuance or
modification of such certificate, the board, upon request of the member, may
modify or correct his prior service certificate.
When membership ceases, such prior service certificate shall become void.
Should the employee again become a member, such employee shall enter the
retirement system as an employee not entitled to prior service credit.
Creditable service at retirement on which the retirement allowance of a member
shall be based shall consist of the membership service rendered by him since he
last became a member, also, if he has a prior service certificate which is in
full force and effect, the amount of the service certified on his prior service
certificate.
(Ord. No. 3590, § 5, 1-3-57)
Sec. 6-52. - Retirement of employees; age or service.
(a)   Any member in service may file his written application to the board
setting forth at what time, not less than thirty (30) days nor more than ninety
(90) days subsequent to the execution of the filing thereof, he desires to be
retired provided such member at the time so specified for his retirement shall
have thirty (30) years of service credit, or attained the age of sixty (60)
years and have been continuously employed by the urban county government for a
period of at least twenty (20) years.
(b)   Any member who has attained the age of seventy (70) years shall be
forthwith retired, or on the first day of the calendar month next succeeding
that in which such member shall have attained an age of seventy (70) years. On
recommendation of the board, the mayor may permit an employee who has attained
the age of seventy (70) years to continue in the employment of the urban county
government for a period not to exceed two (2) years. At the expiration of any
such period, on the recommendation of the board, the mayor may again permit his
continuing for a similar period.
(c)   Any member in service on or after December 1, 1973, may file his written
application to the board setting forth at what time, not less than thirty (30)
days nor more than ninety (90) days subsequent to the execution of the filing
thereof, he desires to be retired, provided such member at the time so
specified for his retirement shall have been continuously employed by the urban
county government for a period of at ten (10) years and shall have attained the
age of forty-five (45). If such member is not age sixty (60), the pension
calculated in accordance with section
6-53 shall become payable beginning with the month that such retired member
attains age sixty (60), if then living. In lieu of such pension, the member,
provided he has then attained age fifty-five (55), may request in writing that
his pension commence not less than thirty (30) days after the date of such
request, in which event the pension payments shall begin in an amount equal to
that calculated in section
6-53 but the total pension so calculated shall be permanently reduced by two-
thirds ( 2/3 ) of one (1) percent for each month by which the commencement
month precedes the month in which the member attains age sixty (60). If the
retired member dies prior to the date payments commence hereunder, the only
death benefit payable shall be the refund of his contributions as provided in
section
6-59(b). If the retired member becomes disabled prior to the date payments
commence hereunder, the disability allowances provided herein shall not be
applicable.
(Ord. No. 3590, § 6, 1-3-57; Ord. No. 305-73, § 2, 12-27-73; Ord. No. 90-92, §
2, 6-25-92)
Sec. 6-53. - Pensions on retirement.
(a)   Upon application of a qualified member for retirement from service on and
after December 1, 1973, the board shall retire such member; and such member
shall receive a pension monthly equal to two and one-half (2½) percent of his
average monthly salary based over the period of three (3) highest years' salary
he received while employed by the urban county government or its predecessor,
the City of Lexington, such amount multiplied by his completed years of service
up to a maximum of twenty (20) years, plus one (1) percent additional allowance
for each year of service in excess of twenty (20), not to exceed sixty-five
(65) percent of three (3) highest years' salary received.
(b)   (1)   When a member, retiring after July 1, 1981, has been retired for
one (1) year or has attained sixty-one (61) years of age, whichever is later,
or when he would have been retired for one (1) year or attained sixty-one (61)
years of age in the event the member is deceased, the board shall increase his
retirement annuity or the annuity paid to his widow or dependent children by
three (3) percent per year, compounded annually; and such increase shall be
granted annually thereafter by the board.
(2)   Beginning July 1, 1992, the board shall grant annual cost-of-living
increases of three (3) percent, compounded annually to the members who retired
prior to July 1, 1981, or their survivors in the same manner as provided in
paragraph (1) of this subsection (b).
(3)   Notwithstanding the provisions of subsections (b)(1) and (2), any member
who retires under disability shall not be entitled to an increase in his
retirement annuity, or in the event he is deceased, in the annuity paid his
widow or dependent children, until the date upon which the member would have
been retired for one (1) year or the date upon which he has attained sixty-one
(61) years of age, whichever is later, or would have attained sixty-one (61)
years of age in the event the member is deceased. Thereafter, the annuity paid
to the member or to his widow or to the guardian of his minor children shall be
increased as provided in subsection (b)(1) of this section.
(4)   (a)   In the first pay period following January 1, 2014, all persons
receiving a pension benefit shall be paid a one-time supplement as follows
based on the amount of pension benefit being received on that date:

Sec. 6-54. - Ordinary disability retirement allowances.
Upon application of a member in service, or of the head of his department, any
member who has had ten (10) or more years of creditable service from February
1, 1939, may be retired by the board not less than thirty (30) and not more
than ninety (90) days next following the date of filing such application, on an
ordinary disability retirement allowance, provided the member shall submit to a
medical examination by a doctor of the board's choice, and provided such doctor
shall certify that such member is mentally or physically incapacitated for the
further performance of duty and such incapacity is likely to be permanent and
such member should be retired. Such member shall receive monthly a pension
equal to one-fortieth of his average monthly salary based on the three (3)
highest years' salary received, multiplied by the number of years' service with
the city, based on a minimum of ten (10) years' service and a maximum of twenty
(20) years' service. Also, there shall be a one (1) percent additional
allowance for each year's service in excess of twenty (20). In no event,
however, shall this monthly pension exceed sixty-five (65) percent of his
average monthly salary based on the three (3) highest years' salary received.
(Ord. No. 3590, § 8, 1-3-57; Ord. No. 4066, § 2, 6-23-60; Ord. No. 113-81, § 1,
7-2-81)
Sec. 6-55. - Accidental disability retirement allowance.
Upon application of a member of the head of his department, any member who has
been totally and permanently incapacitated for duty as the natural and
proximate result of an accident occurring while in the actual performance of
duty at some definite time and place, without willful negligence on his part,
shall be retired by the board, provided the medical director, after a medical
examination of such member shall certify that such member is mentally or
physically incapacitated for the further performance of duty and such
incapacity is likely to be permanent and such member should be retired. Such
member who has had less than ten (10) years continuous service shall receive
monthly fifty (50) percent of his average monthly salary, based on the three
(3) highest years' salary received (if the member has worked as many as three
(3) years; members with less than three (3) years prorated accordingly) and
members with ten (10) years or more at continuous service shall receive monthly
five (5) percent of his average monthly salary based on the three (3) highest
years' salary multiplied by the number of years of continuous service of such
member with the urban county government since February 1, 1939. In no event,
however, shall such member's total allowance exceed sixty-five (65) percent of
his average monthly salary based on the three (3) highest years' salary
received.
(Ord. No. 3590, § 9, 1-3-57; Ord. No. 4066, § 3, 6-23-60; Ord. No. 54-69, § 1,
3-13-69)
Sec. 6-56. - Ordinary death benefits.
(a)   Upon receipt of proper proof by the board of the death of a member in
service or if a member should die while he is on pension, there shall be paid
the following amount to his widow, if there be one, for such length of time as
she remains unmarried, such payments to start immediately for widows with minor
children under the age of eighteen (18) years and age forty-five (45) if there
are no children under eighteen (18); the widow shall receive a monthly pension
in an amount equal to one and one-half (1½) percent of the average monthly
salary for each year of service of the member, based on an average of the three
(3) highest years' salary received by the member, computed on a minimum of ten
(10) years' service or a maximum of thirty (30) years' service or seventy-five
(75) percent of the last monthly annuity of a retired member, whichever is
greater; and in no event shall the pension to the widow be less than one
hundred dollars ($100.00) per month.
(b)   If the member has minor children under the age of eighteen (18) years,
there shall be paid to these children immediately a monthly pension as follows:
(1)   If there be one (1) child, the child shall receive a monthly pension of
one-half the amount to which the widow would have been entitled.
(2)   If there be two (2) children, the children shall receive three-fourths of
the amount to which the widow would have been entitled, share and share alike.
(3)   If there be more than two (2) children, the children shall receive the
full amount to which the widow would have been entitled.
In no event shall the total pension to widow and children exceed sixty-five
(65) percent of the members' average monthly salary based on the three (3)
highest years' salary received by the member as prescribed in subsection (a).
(c)   All pension benefits payable to children shall be discontinued when they
reach the age of eighteen (18) years.
(d)   If there be no widow or children, and the member leaves surviving him a
dependent mother and/or father the dependent mother and/or father of the member
shall be entitled to receive a pension in the same amount as that to which the
widow would have been entitled, share and share alike.
(e)   The widower of a member who is entitled to pension benefits shall receive
the same pension benefits as a widow.
(f)   Any pension benefits being paid to a widow or widower of a member shall
be discontinued if the widow or widower remarries.
(g)   If there be no beneficiaries under subsection (a), (b), (d) or (e) of
this section, the amount which would have been paid under the aforementioned
sections shall be paid as provided in section
6-59(b).
(Ord. No. 3590, § 10, 1-3-57; Ord. No. 4066, § 4, 6-23-60; Ord. No. 54-69, § 2,
3-13-69; Ord. No. 90-92, § 4, 6-25-92; Ord. No. 256-93, § 1, 12-9-93; Ord. No.
63-96, § 1, 5-2-96; Ord. No. 235-96, § 1, 11-21-96)
Sec. 6-57. - Accidental death benefits.
If, upon receipt of proper proof by the board of the death of a member in
service indicating that such death was the natural and proximate result of an
accident occurring at some definite time and place while the member was in the
actual performance of duty, and the board shall decide that the death was the
result of an accident in the performance of duty and not caused by willful
negligence on the part of the member, there shall be paid:
(a)   To the widow, if there be a widow, to continue during her widowhood, a
monthly pension in the amount of fifty (50) percent of the member's average
monthly salary, based on the three (3) highest years' salary received (if the
member had worked as many as three (3) years; members with less than three (3)
years prorated accordingly).
(b)   In addition to benefits in subsection (a), if minor children under age
eighteen (18) also survive, the monthly payment to the widow shall be increased
by ten (10) percent of the aforementioned salary on account of each minor child
payable until they reach age eighteen (18). In no event shall the combined
payments for widow and children exceed seventy-five (75) percent of the
member's average monthly salary calculated as set forth above.
(c)   If the member does not leave a widow, or if she remarries and minor
children under age eighteen (18) exist, each child shall be entitled to a
payment of fifteen (15) percent of the member's average monthly salary
calculated as set forth above until said child reaches eighteen (18) years of
age. In no event shall the combined payments to minor children exceed fifty
(50) percent of the aforementioned salary.
(d)   If neither a widow or minor children survive the member, each dependent
parent, if any, is entitled to a payment of twenty-five (25) percent of the
member's salary as calculated above or fifty (50) percent to both parents who
were dependent upon the member.
(e)   If there be no beneficiaries under the above subsections, the amount
which would have been paid out under such subsections shall be paid as provided
in section
6-59(b).
(Ord. No. 3590, § 11, 1-3-57; Ord. No. 54-69, § 3, 3-13-69)
Sec. 6-58. - Workmen's compensation payments deducted from benefits.
Any amounts which may be paid or payable under the provisions of any state
workmen's compensation or similar law to a member or to the dependents of a
member on account of any disability or death while in the service of the urban
county government shall be offset against and payable in lieu of any benefits
payable out of funds provided by the urban county government under the
provisions of the retirement system on account of the same disability or death.
In case the present value of the total computed benefits under such workmen's
compensation or similar law is less than the pension reserve or the benefits
otherwise payable from the pension fund, the present value of the computed
payments shall be deducted from the pension benefits; and such benefits as may
be provided by this division, so reduced, shall be payable under the provisions
of this division.
(Ord. No. 3590, § 12, 1-3-57)
Sec. 6-59. - Return of employee contributions.
(a)   Should a member discontinue to be an employee on or after December 1,
1973, where no immediate or deferred benefits are payable, or should a member
who is entitled to deferred benefits hereunder at the time of discontinuance
elect in writing filed with the board to forfeit his deferred benefit, such
member shall be paid the total amount of his accumulated contribution reduced
by any prior allowances paid to him or on his behalf. The member's refund may
be transferred directly, at the member's request, to the trustee of an eligible
retirement plan pursuant to 26 USC § 401(A)(31).
(b)   If, at the death of a retired member who retired on or after December 1,
1973, or at the death of his spouse or other dependent receiving benefits
hereunder, no further benefits of any sort are payable from the pension fund,
and if the total benefits paid to the member or on his behalf to his
beneficiaries are less than the total amount of his accumulated contributions,
such difference shall be paid to the estate of the member or, if death benefits
were being paid hereunder to a beneficiary, to the estate of that beneficiary.
(c)   All amounts payable under this section shall be payable in a lump sum and
shall be payable as soon as reasonably possible.
(Ord. No. 3590, § 13, 1-3-57; Ord. No. 305-73, § 4, 12-27-73; Ord. No. 178-81,
§ 1, 10-15-81; Ord. No. 50-93, § 12, 4-3-93)
Sec. 6-60. - Reexamination of disability beneficiaries; gainful occupation;
restoration to service.
(a)   Once each year during the first five (5) years following retirement of a
member on a retirement allowance for disability, and once in every three-year
period thereafter, the board may, and upon his application shall, require any
disability beneficiary who has not yet attained sixty (60) years of age to
undergo a medical examination to be made by the medical director at the place
of residence of said beneficiary or other place mutually agreed upon. Should
any disability beneficiary who has not yet attained the age of sixty (60) years
refuse to submit to at least one (1) medical examination in any such year by
the medical director, his allowance may be discontinued until his withdrawal of
such refusal; and should his refusal continue for one (1) year, all his rights
in and to his pension may be revoked by the board.
(b)   Should the medical director report and certify to the board that such
disability beneficiary is engaged in or is able to engage in a gainful
occupation paying more than the difference between his retirement allowance and
the average monthly salary of such beneficiary before his retirement and should
the board concur in such reports, the amounts of his pension shall be reduced
to an amount which, together with his pension and the amount earnable by him,
shall equal the amount of his or her average monthly salary while in the
service of the urban county government. Should the earning capacity be later
changed, the amount of his pension may be further modified in like manner.
(c)   Should a disability beneficiary be restored to active service at a
compensation not less than his average monthly salary with the urban county
government when he retired, his retirement allowance shall cease and he shall
again become a member of the retirement system and he shall contribute
thereafter at the current rate determined by the board of trustees. Any prior
service certificate, on the basis of which his service was computed at the time
of his retirement, shall be restored to full force and effect, if he be
restored before the attainment of the age of sixty (60) years; and, in
addition, upon his subsequent retirement he shall be credited with all his
service as a member.
(Ord. No. 3590, § 14, 1-3-57)
Sec. 6-61. - Legal advisers.
The commissioner of law and his assistants shall be the legal advisers of the
board.
(Ord. No. 3590, § 15, 1-3-57)
Sec. 6-62. - Medical director.
The board shall designate a physician as medical director who is not eligible
to participate in the retirement system. The medical director shall arrange for
and pass upon all medical examinations required under the provisions of this
division, shall investigate all essential statements and certificates by or on
behalf of a member in connection with application for disability retirement,
and shall report in writing to the board his conclusion and recommendations
upon all matters referred to him.
(Ord. No. 3590, § 16, 1-3-57)
Sec. 6-63. - Benefits; contributions prerequisite.
No retirement benefits or allowances or pensions shall be paid to any member of
the retirement system who has not paid in to the pension fund his assessment on
his average monthly salary for at least ten (10) years except as is
specifically provided for in sections
6-55,
6-57,
6-59 and
6-64.
(Ord. No. 3590, § 17, 1-3-57)
Sec. 6-64. - Funeral expenses.
Upon receipt of the proper proof of the death of a member or retired employee
of the retirement system, the board shall, in addition to any allowance or
benefit set out herein, pay an amount not to exceed seven thousand five hundred
dollars ($7,500.00) to the funeral director having charge of the funeral of
such deceased member for the actual costs of the funeral.
(Ord. No. 3590, § 18, 1-3-57; Ord. No. 4066, § 5, 6-23-60; Ord. No. 11-99, § 1,
1-28-99; Ord. No. 273-2008, § 1, 12-9-08)
Sec. 6-65. - Benefits; beneficiaries, specified.
(a)   No person shall be entitled to receive any pension or other allowance
from the pension fund except a retired member, a widow, children under the age
of eighteen (18) years, any dependent mother and/or father, the estate of any
of the above-named or the funeral benefits herein set out.
(b)   The monthly pension benefits of each retired member, widow, child under
the age of eighteen (18) years, or dependent mother and father who is receiving
benefits under chapter 6 of this Code shall be increased by the sum of thirty
dollars ($30.00) on January 9, 2001, in addition to the previous increases of
forty dollars ($40.00) made on January 1, 1998 and on October 1, 1999,
notwithstanding any other provision of chapter 6 of this Code.
(Ord. No. 3590, § 19, 1-3-57; Ord. No. 305-73, § 5, 12-27-73; Ord. No. 262-97,
§ 1, 12-11-97, Ord. No. 273-99, § 1, 9-23-99; Ord. No. 106-2001, § 1, 5-3-01)
Sec. 6-66. - Pension fund, books or accounts, bond of custodian, payments from
fund.
The commissioner of finance shall be the custodian of the pension fund and
shall securely and safely keep the same subject to the control and direction of
the board, and shall keep the books and accounts concerning such fund in such a
manner as may be prescribed by the board; and the books and accounts shall
always be subject to the inspection of the board or any member thereof; and
such books shall at all times show the total contributions to such pension fund
of any member derived from the assessment on such member's salary.
The bond of the commissioner of finance acting as such shall run to and be for
the benefit of the pension fund for the faithful performance of the duties of
the office and that the commissioner of finance will safely keep and well and
trustfully account for all moneys and property which come into his hands as
custodian of the pension fund and that he will, upon expiration of his office,
surrender and deliver to his successor all bonds, securities and unexpended
moneys or properties which may have come into his hands as treasurer of such
fund.
All moneys ordered to be paid from the pension fund to any person shall be paid
by the commissioner of finance upon a warrant or order duly signed by the
chairman of the board of trustees and countersigned by the secretary thereof,
and no warrant or order shall be drawn except by the order of the board as
having been duly entered on the record of the proceedings of the board.
The board may retain and pay for professional investment counseling services
and professional banking custodial services. The commissioner of finance shall
transmit assets of the fund to and from investment counselors and custodial
banks as directed by the board.
(Ord. No. 3590, § 20, 1-3-57; Ord. No. 205-72, § 2, 9-28-72; Ord. No. 90-92, §
5, 6-25-92)
Sec. 6-67. - Application of pension or retirement system.
Nothing in this division shall be construed as interfering with or affecting
any way or manner, expressly or by implication, or otherwise, with any other
department of the urban county government that is now and has been operating
under the civil service pension fund plan; and it is the distinct intention of
this division to separate and to keep apart from the laws governing those
departments heretofore being operated under the civil service pension fund plan
as prescribed and enumerated in KRS 95.851 and KRS 61.510 et seq., from the
provisions of this division.
(Ord. No. 3590, § 21, 1-3-57)
Sec. 6-68. - Members of the system; contributions as acceptance of ordinances;
contracts status.
Only those employees of the urban county government who were included in the
classified service of the City of Lexington on December 31, 1973, and who chose
to stay under the pension system created by Ordinance No. 3590, as amended,
shall be members of the retirement system; and upon the effective date of the
civil service provisions and this division all members of the retirement system
shall pay monthly into the pension fund the percentage of his monthly salary as
prescribed by ordinance; and the payments of such assessment by such member
into the pension fund shall be deemed an acceptance of the terms and provisions
of the civil service provisions and of this division and shall constitute and
thereby make effective a contract between such member and employee and the
urban county government, which contract shall be inviolable and shall continue
to exist without right of revisions or repeal as between the urban county
government and such member or employee unless by the mutual agreement of such
employee and the urban county government.
(Ord. No. 3590, § 22, 1-3-57)
Sec. 6-69. - Contributions from members—Amount for 1956 and thereafter.
(a)   In accordance with the provisions of the civil service provisions of the
urban county government, and retirement system or pension fund provisions of
the urban county government, there is hereby assessed against each employee of
the civil service of the urban county government under the terms and provisions
of such civil service provisions, and against each member of the retirement
system, under the provisions and terms of the retirement system or pension fund
provisions, a three (3) percent contribution of his monthly salary. Such sum is
to be paid to the commissioner of finance each month by each of such employees
and placed by the commissioner in the pension fund, as provided in such pension
fund provisions. Such sum shall be deducted from the salary checks of the
employees and paid into such fund until the employees shall otherwise request.
(b)   This division shall remain in full force and effect for the year 1957 and
for each succeeding year unless amended or repealed in any succeeding year;
those persons receiving pension benefits as of June 30, 1960, shall draw the
same benefits under the provisions of Ordinance No. 1018 as amended by
Ordinance No. 2479 and under the provisions of Ordinance No. 3590 [
division 2 of this article].
(Ord. No. 3590, § 23, 1-3-57; Ord. No. 4066, § 6, 6-23-60; Ord. No. 90-92, § 6,
6-25-92)
Sec. 6-69.1. - Same—Amount beginning July 1, 1969; amount beginning January l,
1970.
Pursuant to KRS 90.400 and section
6-49 of this Code, the percentum of salary to be withheld from civil service
employees for the benefit of their pension fund shall, beginning July 1, 1969,
be four (4) percent of the monthly salary of each such employee, and beginning
January 1, 1970, five (5) percent of the monthly salary of each such employee.
(Ord. No. 106-69, § 1, 4-24-69)
Sec. 6-69.2. - Same—Amount beginning July 1, 1981.
Pursuant to KRS 67A.320 and section
6-69 of this Code of Ordinances, the percentum of salary to be withheld from
members for the benefit of their pension fund shall be, beginning the first pay
period commencing after July 1, 1981, eight (8) percent of the monthly salary
of each such member.
(Ord. No. 350-73, § 6, 12-27-73; Ord. No. 110-81, § 1, 7-2-81)
Sec. 6-69.2.1. Same—Amount beginning August 1, 1992.
Pursuant to KRS 67A.320 and section
6-69 of this Code of Ordinances, the percentum of salary to be withheld from
members for the benefit of their pension fund shall be, beginning the first pay
period commencing after August 1, 1992, eight and one-half (8½) percent of the
monthly salary of each such member.
(Ord. No. 90-92, § 7, 6-25-92)
Sec. 6-69.3. - Contributions from the urban county government.
(a)   For the period July 1, 1981, to June 30, 1982, the urban county
government shall contribute to the pension fund an amount equal to fourteen
(14) percent of the monthly salary of each member.
(b)   Beginning July 1, 1982, the urban county government shall contribute to
the pension fund an amount equal to sixteen (16) percent of the monthly salary
of each member.
(c)   Beginning July 1, 1992, the urban county government shall contribute to
the pension fund an amount equal to seventeen and one-half (17½) percent of the
monthly salary of each member.
(d)   The urban county government shall contribute to the pension fund
additional amounts necessary to fund on an actuarially sound basis the benefits
promised or described in the fund pursuant to KRS 67A.320.
(Ord. No. 350-73, § 7, 12-27-73; Ord. No. 209-75, § 1, 7-31-75; Ord. No. 110-
81, § 2, 7-2-81; Ord. No. 90-92, § 8, 6-25-92; Ord. No. 19-98, § 1, 1-22-98)
Sec. 6-69.4. - Service credit for unused, accumulated sick leave.
(a)   Any member who retires may purchase service credit for up to seven
hundred twenty (720) hours of unused sick leave accrued while contributing to
the pension fund from which the retirement benefit is to be paid in accordance
with this section.
(b)   A member retiring who chooses to purchase service credit for unused,
accumulated sick leave as provided in this subsection shall notify the pension
board of his intention upon submitting his retirement application to the board.
The urban county government shall certify the retiring member's unused,
accumulated sick leave balance, up to a maximum of seven hundred twenty (720)
hours. The member's sick leave balance, expressed in days, shall be divided by
the average number of working days per month and rounded to the nearest number
of whole months. This number of months shall be added to the member's service
credit for the purpose of determining his rate of retirement annuity pursuant
to section
6-53 through
6-55 and his total service credit pursuant to section
6-52. The value of the unused, accumulated sick leave shall be based on the
daily salary rate calculated from the member's last annual salary. Payment for
unused sick leave, up to a maximum of seven hundred twenty (720) hours, shall
be incorporated into the annual salary of the final year of service, provided
that the member contributes to the pension fund the amount set forth in
sections
6-69 through
6-69.2.1 and the urban county government matches such contribution by the
amount set forth in section
6-69.3 on the unused, accumulated sick leave.
(Ord. No. 124-90, § 1, 6-14-90)
Editor's note(s)—Section 2 of Ord. No. 124-90 declared the provisions effective
retroactive to Jan. 1, 1990.
Sec. 6-69.5. - Group health insurance plan—Members retiring on or after July 1,
1999.
(a)   All members of the city employees pension fund who retire on or after
July 1, 1999, shall be eligible to participate in a group health insurance plan
(providing hospital and medical or health maintenance organization health care
coverage) approved by the urban county council for such retirees (the "plan").
(b)   The urban county government shall provide, on behalf of all members of
the city employees pension fund who retire on or after July 1, 1999 and who
elect to participate in the group health insurance plan coverage provided
pursuant to subsection (a) of this section, the following benefits: (1) for the
period from July 1, 1999 through June 30, 2000, a sum equal to fifty (50)
percent of the urban county government's contribution to the health insurance
component of the benefit pool for current urban county government employees
(the "contribution"); and (2) for the period from July 1, 2000 through June 30,
2001 and thereafter, a sum equal to the single premium for the plan coverage
selected by the retiree, but not more than one hundred (100) percent of the
contribution.
(c)   No benefits shall be available under this section to members of the city
employees pension fund who retire prior to July 1, 1999 or who do not
participate in the group health insurance plan approved by the urban county
council.
(d)   All payments shall be made to the approved provider of the group health
insurance plan, not to the retiree, and the retiree shall not be entitled to
receive any portion of the government contribution remaining after payment is
made to the approved provider.
(e)   Group rates under the group health insurance plan approved by the urban
county council under subsection (a) shall be made available to the spouse,
dependents, and disabled children, regardless of the disabled child's age, of a
qualified and participating retiree, if the premium for the spouse, dependent,
or disabled child is paid by payroll deduction or similar method.
(Ord. No. 198-99, § 1, 7-8-99)
Sec. 6-69.6. - Same—Members retired prior to July 1, 1999.
(a)   All members of the city employees pension fund who retired prior to July
1, 1999, and who did not terminate their participation in the group health
insurance plan provided by the urban county government before that date, shall
continue to be eligible to participate in a group health insurance plan
(providing hospitalization and medical or health maintenance organization
health care coverage) approved by the urban county council for such returnees
(the "plan").
(b)   The urban county government shall provide, on behalf of all members of
the city employees pension fund who retired prior to July 1, 1999 and who were
participants in the group health insurance plan coverage provided to urban
county government employees and retirees immediately prior to July 1, 1999, the
following benefits: (1) for the period from July 1, 1999 through June 30, 2000,
a sum equal to fifty (50) percent of the urban county government's contribution
to the health insurance component of the benefit pool for current urban county
government employees (the "contribution"); and (2) for the period from July 1,
2000 through June 30, 2001 and thereafter, a sum equal to the single premium
for the plan coverage selected by the retiree, but not more than one hundred
(100) percent of the contribution.
(c)   No benefits shall be available under this section to retired members of
the city employees pension fund who were not, immediately prior to July 1,
1999, participants in the group health insurance plan coverage provided to
urban county government employees and retirees.
(d)   All payments shall be made to the approved provider of the group health
insurance plan, not to the retiree, and the retiree shall not be entitled to
receive any portion of the government contribution remaining after payment is
made to the approved provider.
(e)   Group rates under the group health insurance plan approved by the urban
county council under subsection (a) shall be made available to the spouse,
dependents, and disabled children, regardless of the disabled child's age, of a
qualified and participating retiree, if the premium for the spouse, dependent,
or disabled child is paid by payroll deduction or similar method.
(Ord. No. 217-99, § 1, 8-19-99; Ord. No. 366-2000, § 1, 12-5-00)
Sec. 6-70. - Effective date.
This division shall take effect on January 1, 1957.
(Ord. No. 3590, § 24, 1-3-57)
DIVISION 2. - ORDINANCE NUMBER 1018 AND AMENDATORY ORDINANCE NUMBER 2479 4
 
Notes
  Editor's note(s)—Although the contents of this division are superseded by the
4 provisions of div. 1, this division is included for reference as to employees
  receiving benefits hereunder. In the republication of this Code, the original
  language has been retained.
Sec. 6-71. - Definitions.
The following words and phrases as used in this division unless a different
meaning is plainly required by the context shall have the following meanings:
(1)   Employee shall mean all employees of the city who are included within the
city civil service under the provisions of section 6-46.
(2)   The board and the board of trustees shall mean the board of trustees of
the city employees pension fund constituted as provided in section
6-72.
(3)   Pension fund shall mean the moneys derived from assessments deducted from
salaries of the employees, and from the levy of a special tax, either or both,
as provided in section
6-73, or any other sum derived from any other source by gift or otherwise to be
used for the retirement of employees after the prescribed number of years of
service and for the benefit of disabled employees and for the benefit of widows
and dependent children and parents in the case of death of an employee within
the scope of his or her employment according to the terms of this division.
(4)   Prior service shall mean service rendered prior to the first day of
February, 1939, for which credit is allowable under the provisions of sections
6-76 and
6-77.
(5)   Widow shall mean a woman legally married to an employee where, at the
time of death of such employee:
(a)   There has been no decree of divorce entered into dissolving such
marriage; or, if such decree has been entered, it is not in full force and
effect; and
(b)   There has been no decree of divorce from bed and board secured by the
husband; and
(c)   The woman has not voluntarily abandoned her husband.
Sec. 6-72. - Board of trustees; membership; officers; control of pension fund.
(a)   The membership of the board of trustees of the city employees pension
fund shall consist of the mayor and four (4) commissioners of the city. The
mayor shall be chairman of the board. In addition thereto, but without having a
vote on any questions that come before the board, the city clerk shall be ex
officio secretary of the board and the city treasurer shall be the treasurer of
the board.
(b)   The board shall have the exclusive control and management of the pension
fund.
Sec. 6-73. - Contributions from employees; tax by city; investment of funds.
(a)   There is hereby assessed a sufficient percentum of the salary from each
employee's pay so as to adequately maintain the pension fund hereby created,
but in no event shall said assessment exceed five (5) percent of the monthly
salary of each employee. Within such limit, the percentum of salary so withheld
shall be fixed annually by the board of commissioners, and same shall be paid
into the pension fund in cash and held by the treasurer subject to the order of
the board of trustees.
(b)   The board of commissioners shall annually levy a tax not exceeding five
cents ($0.05) on each one hundred dollars ($100.00) valuation of taxable
property in the city, and the proceeds of such tax shall be paid into the
pension fund in cash and held by the treasurer subject to the order of the
board of trustees. In no year shall the contribution of the city by means of
such tax be less than the total amount assessed upon and deducted from the
salary of the employees.
Sec. 6-73.1. - Contributions from employees of department of recreation; tax;
social security for recreation employees.
(a)   Each employee of the department of recreation who is eligible for civil
service as set forth in this Code is hereby assessed a sufficient percentum of
his salary to be paid into the pension fund, but in no event shall said
assessment exceed five (5) percent of the monthly salary of each employee.
Within such limit, the percentum of salary so withheld shall be fixed annually
by the board of commissioners; and same shall be paid into the pension fund in
cash and held by the treasurer subject to the order of the board of trustees.
(b)   The board of commissioners shall annually levy a tax not to exceed five
cents ($0.05) on each one hundred dollars ($100.00) valuation of taxable
property in the city and the proceeds of such tax shall be paid into the
pension fund and held by the treasurer subject to the order of the board of
trustees. This contribution by the city by means of this tax shall be not less
than the total amount assessed upon and deducted from the salaries of the
employees.
(c)   Employees of the department of recreation who are being covered under the
provisions of this section and the civil service plan, and who are now covered
by social security, shall continue to pay social security; and the city shall
continue its contributions for these employees pursuant to the provisions of
KRS 90.400; and this coverage and social security coverage is hereby deemed the
pension plan for employees and classes of employees who are members of the
department of recreation.
(d)   Those department of recreation employees who cannot meet the requirements
of civil service because of age shall remain "probationary employees" of the
city pursuant to KRS 97.445.
(Ord. No. 4153, § 1, 12-22-60)
Sec. 6-74. - Investment of pension fund.
The board of trustees shall have the power to draw such pension fund from the
treasurer and invest the same or any part thereof in the name of the board of
trustees of the city employees pension fund in interest-bearing coupons of the
United States, the State of Kentucky, or any county or city of the first,
second or third class of the State of Kentucky, or in any securities in which
trustees or guardians are permitted to invest trust or guardianship funds under
the laws of the state; and all securities shall be deposited with the treasurer
and shall be subject to the order of the board.
Sec. 6-75. - Regulations of board of trustees; decisions on applications for
pensions, etc.; record.
The board of trustees shall have the power to make all needful rules and
regulations for its government in the discharge of its duties. It shall hear
and decide all applications for relief, pension or retirement allowance under
this division, and its decision on any such application shall be final and
conclusive and not subject to revision or reversal, except by the board. A
record shall be kept of all meetings and proceedings of the board.
Sec. 6-76. - Prior service; prior service certificates.
Prior service certificates duly issued to employees respecting service as an
employee prior to February 1, 1939, shall be final and conclusive for
retirement purposes as to such service. When the holder of such certificate
ceases to be in the employ of the city because of resignation, or discharge for
cause, his certificate shall become void; and should he again become an
employee he shall not be entitled to credit for such prior service.
Sec. 6-77. - Creditable service at retirement.
Creditable service at retirement, on which the retirement allowance of an
employee shall be based, shall consist of the amount of service rendered by him
since he last became an employee and also, if he has a prior service
certificate which is in full force and effect, the amount of service certified
thereon.
Sec. 6-78. - Retirement of employees; age and service.
(a)   Any employee in service may file his written application to the board
specifying at what time, not less than thirty (30) days subsequent to the
execution and filing thereof, he desires to be retired, provided such employee
at the time so specified for his retirement shall have attained the age of
sixty (60) years and shall have been continuously employed by the city for a
period of at least twenty (20) years.
(b)   Any employee who has attained the age of seventy (70) years shall be
retired forthwith or on the first day of the calendar month next succeeding
that in which such employee shall have attained the age of seventy (70) years.
On recommendation of the board the city manager may permit an employee who has
attained the age of seventy (70) years to continue in the employment of the
city for a period not to exceed two (2) years. At the expiration of any such
period on the recommendation of the board the city manager may again permit his
continuing for a similar period.
Sec. 6-79. - Pensions on retirement; amount.
Upon the application of an employee for retirement from service, pursuant to
section
6-78(a), the board, if it sees fit, may retire such employee. If his service as
an employee shall have existed continuously for as much as twenty (20) years
after February 1, 1939, such employee shall receive a pension monthly equal to
one-half of his average monthly salary based on the highest five (5) annual
salaries received during the ten-year period next preceding date of retirement.
In the event such employee continuously for more than ten (10) years from and
after February 1, 1939, but less than twenty (20) years from and after that
date, and his prior service certificate is credited with a sufficient number of
years, when added to his subsequent continuous service from and after February
1, 1939, to bring his total continuous service to twenty (20) years, such
employee shall receive a pension monthly equal to one-half of his average
monthly salary based on the ten-year period next preceding date of retirement.
In no event, however, shall a monthly pension exceed one-half of the monthly
salary of the employee at the time of his retirement.
Sec. 6-80. - Ordinary disability retirement allowances.
Upon the application of an employee or of the head of his department, any
employee who has had ten (10) or more years of creditable service after
February 1, 1939, may be retired by the board not less than thirty (30) and not
more than ninety (90) days next following the date of filing such application
on an ordinary disability retirement allowance provided the medical director,
after a medical examination of such employee, shall certify that such employee
is mentally or physically incapacitated for the further performance of duty,
and such incapacity is likely to be permanent and such employee should be
retired. Such employee shall receive such proportion of the pension allowance
to which he would be entitled if retiring under the provisions of section
6-79 as his number of years service since February 1, 1939, together with the
years credited to him on his prior service certificate (provided such
certificate is in full force and effect under section
6-76) bear to twenty (20) years; provided, that in no event shall his allowance
exceed one-half of his monthly salary at the time of his retirement.
Sec. 6-81. - Accidental disability retirement allowance.
Upon application of an employee, or of the head of his department, any employee
who has been totally and permanently incapacitated for duty as the natural and
proximate result of an accident occurring while in the actual performance of
duty at some definite time and place, without willful negligence on his part,
shall be retired by the board, provided the medical director after a medical
examination of such employee shall certify that such employee is mentally and
physically incapacitated for the further performance of duty and such
incapacity is likely to be permanent and such employee should be retired. Such
employee shall receive monthly one-twentieth of his average monthly salary
during the period of his employment or during the ten-year period preceding the
date of retirement, whichever is the shorter period, multiplied by the number
of years of continuous service of such employee with the city since February 1,
1939. If such employee has a prior service certificate, he shall receive
monthly in addition one-fortieth of his average monthly salary multiplied by
the number of years credited to him on such certificate, provided his
certificate is in full force and effect under the provisions of section
6-76. In no event, however, shall such employee's total allowance exceed one-
half of his monthly salary at the time of his retirement.
Sec. 6-82. - Ordinary death benefits.
Upon the receipt of proper proofs by the board of the death of an employee,
while in service, which is not the result of an accident in the actual
performance of duty, as defined in section
6-83, there shall be paid the following amounts, at the rate of thirty dollars
($30.00) per month, to his widow, if there be one, for such length of time as
she remains unmarried; and if there be no widow or if she should remarry, then
to his infant children to be divided equally between them until any such child
reaches the age of fifteen (15) years, then to the survivors under that age,
and if there be neither widow unmarried nor infant children under fifteen (15)
years of age; then to the dependent father and mother to be divided equally
between them and if either be dead, to the survivor:
(1)   A benefit equal to the sum of the total compensation received by the
employee during the two (2) years immediately preceding his death, if the
employee has been in the continuous service of the city for twenty (20) years
or more after February 1, 1939; or
(2)   A benefit equal to one-twentieth of the sum of the total compensation
received by the employee during the two (2) years immediately preceding his
death, multiplied by the number of years continuous service if the employee had
been in continuous service of the city for less than twenty (20) years after
February 1, 1939; plus, if such employee had a prior service certificate in
full force and effect under section
6-76, an additional benefit of one-fortieth of such two (2) years' salary
multiplied by the number of years credited on such certificate; provided, in no
event, shall there be allowed a benefit hereunder greater than the sum total of
such employee's two years' salary; and
(3)   In addition to (1) or (2), as the case may be, the accumulated
contributions of the deceased employee to the pension fund.
Sec. 6-83. - Accidental death benefits.
If, upon the receipt of proper proofs by the board of the death of an employee
in service indicating that such death was the natural and proximate result of
an accident occurring at some definite time and place while the employee was in
the actual performance of duty, the board shall decide that the death was the
result of an accident in the performance of duty and not caused by willful
negligence on the part of the employee, there shall be paid as benefits the
amount of his accumulated contribution in a lump sum, plus a pension of thirty
dollars ($30.00) per month as follows:
(1)   To his widow, if there be a widow, to continue during her widowhood; or
(2)   If there be no widow or the widow dies or remarries, then to his child or
children, under the age of fifteen (15) years, if he leaves children, divided
equally between or among such children and to continue as a joint and
survivorship pension for the benefit of the child or children under such age
until every child dies or attains such age; or
(3)   If there be no widow or the widow dies or remarries, and if there be no
child or children under the age of fifteen (15) years surviving such deceased
employee, then to his dependent mother and father, or if either be dead then to
the other, to continue for life.
(4)   If there be no beneficiary under (1), (2) or (3), then the amount which
would have been paid under this section shall remain part of the pension fund
and shall be credited to the pension accumulated fund.
Sec. 6-84. - Workmen's compensation payments deducted from benefits.
Any amounts which may be paid or payable under the provisions of any state
workmen's compensation or similar law to an employee or to the dependents of an
employee on account of disability or death while in the service of the city
shall be offset against and payable in lieu of any benefit payable out of funds
provided by the city under the provisions of this division on account of the
same disability or death. In case the present value of the total computed
benefits under such workmen's compensation or similar law is less than the
pension reserve on the benefits otherwise payable from the pension fund
pursuant to this division, then the present value of the computed payments
shall be deducted from the pension benefits, and such benefits as may be
provided by this division, so reduced, shall be payable as provided in this
division.
Sec. 6-85. - Termination of employment; return of employee's contributions.
Should an employee discontinue to be an employee of the city except by death,
or retirement under the provisions of this division, he shall be paid one-half
of the amount of the accumulated contributions standing to the credit of his
individual account in the pension fund after two (2) years; provided, if such
employee has during his employment received any disability allowance from the
pension fund, such allowance shall be offset and deducted from the amount of
the accumulated contributions; and one-half the balance only of such
contributions shall be paid to such employee after two (2) years. Any employee
who shall have charges preferred against him, which charges shall be of such
nature as to merit dismissal from service under the provisions of section 6-43,
may resign and accept the benefits above provided in this section. However, if
such employee elects to stand trial, and if the result of the hearing is
dismissal from service, such employee shall not receive any accumulated
contributions or any other allowances or benefits from the pension fund. No
accumulated contributions shall be returned to any employee not serving for as
much as two (2) years after February 1, 1939.
Sec. 6-86. - Reexamination of disability beneficiaries; gainful occupation;
restoration to city service.
(a)   Once each year during the first five (5) years following retirement of an
employee on a retirement allowance for disability, and once in every three-year
period thereafter, the board may, and upon his application shall, require any
such disability beneficiary who has not yet attained the age of sixty (60)
years to undergo a medical examination, such examination to be made by the
medical director at the place of residence of such beneficiary or other place
mutually agreed upon. Should any disability beneficiary who has not yet
attained the age of sixty (60) years refuse to submit to at least one (1)
medical examination in any such year by the medical director, his allowance may
be discontinued by the board until his withdrawal of such refusal; and, should
his refusal continue for one (1) year, all his rights in and to his pension may
be revoked by the board.
(b)   Should the medical director report and certify to the board that such
disability beneficiary is engaged in or is able to engage in a gainful
occupation paying more than the difference between his retirement allowance and
his average monthly salary before his retirement, and should the board concur
in such report, the amount of his pension shall be reduced to an amount which,
together with the amount earnable by him, shall equal the amount of his average
monthly salary while in the service of the city. Should the earning capacity of
such beneficiary be later changed, the amount of his pension may be further
modified in like manner.
(c)   Should a disability beneficiary be restored to active service at a
compensation not less than his average monthly salary with the city when he
retired, his retirement allowance shall cease and he shall again become an
employee and shall contribute thereafter at the same rate as if he had not been
retired. Any prior service certificate, on the basis of which his service was
computed at the time of his retirement, shall be restored to full force and
effect, if he be restored before the attainment of age sixty (60) years; and,
in addition, upon his subsequent retirement he shall be credited with all his
services as an employee.
Sec. 6-87. - Legal advisers.
The city attorney and his assistant shall be the legal advisers of the board.
Sec. 6-89. - Medical director.
The board shall designate a physician as medical director who is not eligible
to participate in the retirement system. The medical director shall arrange for
and pass upon all medical examinations required under the provisions of this
division, shall investigate all essential statements and certificates by or on
behalf of an employee in connection with the application for a disability
retirement, and shall report in writing to the board his conclusions and
recommendations upon all the matters referred to him.
Sec. 6-89. - Benefits; contributions prerequisite.
No retirement benefits or allowances or pensions shall be paid to any employee
who has not paid into the pension fund the assessment on his average monthly
salary for at least ten (10) years except as specifically provided for in
sections
6-81,
6-83,
6-85 and
6-90.
Sec. 6-90. - Funeral expenses.
Whenever an employee or retired employee shall die, the board of trustees may,
in addition to any other allowance or benefit provided in this division, pay
not exceeding one hundred dollars ($100.00) to the undertaker having charge of
the funeral of such deceased employee.
Sec. 6-91. - Benefits; beneficiaries, specified.
Except as provided in section
6-90, no person shall be entitled to receive any pension or other allowance
from the pension fund except a retired employee, his widow, his children under
the age of fifteen (15) years or his dependent mother or father.
Sec. 6-92. - Pension fund; custody; books or accounts; bond of custodian;
payments from fund.
The city treasurer shall be the custodian of the pension fund, and shall
securely and safely keep the same subject to the control and direction of the
board of trustees, and shall keep the books and accounts concerning such fund
in such manner as may be prescribed by the board. Such books and accounts shall
always be subject to the inspection of the board or any member thereof, and
such books shall at all times show the total contributions to such pension fund
of any employee derived from the assessment on such employee's salary.
The bond of the city treasurer acting as such shall run to and be for the
benefit of the pension fund, for the faithful performance of the duties of the
office, and that he will safely keep and well and trustfully account for all
money and property which may come into his hands as treasurer of the pension
fund and that he will, upon the expiration of his office, surrender and deliver
to his successor all bonds, securities and unexpended money or properties which
may have come into his hands as treasurer of such fund. All money ordered to be
paid from the pension fund to any person shall be paid by the treasurer upon a
warrant or order duly signed by the chairman of the board of trustees and
countersigned by the secretary thereof, and no warrant or order shall be drawn
except by the order of the board of trustees as having been duly entered on the
record of the proceedings of the board.
Sec. 6-93. - Members of pension and retirement system.
Only those employees of the city who are included in the civil service of the
city under the provisions of section 6-46 shall be members of the pension and
retirement system provided in this division.
Sec. 6-94. - Contributions to pension fund during probationary period.
Any appointee to a permanent position shall, during the term of his
probationary period, contribute to the pension fund and be eligible to the
rights and privileges provided in this division.
Sec. 6-95. - Inviolability of contract between city and civil service
employees.
This section number is included for the purpose of referring to KRS 90.400(2)
(b) which, paraphrased, provides that the adoption of an ordinance creating a
pension fund, followed by acceptance from employees of a portion of their
wages, and the levying of a tax, creates an inviolable contract between the
city and its employees; and they shall continue to operate under civil service,
even a repeal of the ordinance not affecting the employees without their
consent.
Sec. 6-96. - Time spent in armed forces counts for pension purposes.
All time spent in the armed forces of the United States by any civil service
employee of the city at any time after becoming such an employee shall be
counted for all purposes in connection with the provisions of this division as
regular time of employment by the city the same as if the employee had not been
absent from his duties with the city during the time spent in the armed forces,
provided such employee returns to his or her regular employment with the city
within sixty (60) days after his or her discharge from the armed forces.
Sec. 6-97. - Amount of assessment.
(a)   Pursuant to the provisions of KRS 90.400(1) and section
6-73 hereof, the assessment for the pension fund against each employee shall be
two (2) percent of his or her monthly salary, until changed by ordinance.
(b)   Pursuant to KRS 90.400 and section
6-49 of the Lexington Code of Ordinances, the percentum of salary to be
withheld from civil service employees for the benefit of their pension fund
shall, beginning July 1, 1969, be four (4) percent of the monthly salary of
each such employee, and beginning January 1, 1970, five (5) percent of the
monthly salary of each such employee.
(Ord. No. 106-69, § 1, 4-24-69)
Sec. 6-98. - Nonapplication to police and fire and emergency services
divisions.
Nothing in this division shall be construed as interfering with or affecting in
any way or manner, expressly, by implication, or otherwise the police or fire
and emergency services division of the city; and it is the distinct intention
of this division to separate and keep apart from the provisions of this
division those departments, which shall continue to be operated under the
police and firemen's pension fund plan, pursuant to the provisions of KRS
95.520 et sequitur.

  6-47 et seq.; licenses,

ARTICLE I. - IN GENERAL 2
 
Notes
2 Editor's note(s)—The editor has designated the existing provisions of ch. 7 as
  art. I to accommodate the inclusion of Ord. No. 156-82 as art. II.
Sec. 7-1. - Commissioner of finance.
The commissioner of finance shall control the department of finance and shall,
under the direction of the mayor and council, have general supervision over the
affairs and work of such department. That department shall be responsible for
the custody, investment and disbursement of all funds of the urban county
government in accordance with the procedures and standards established by the
council.
(Ord. No. 156-70, § 2, 7-9-70; Ord. No. 32-72, § 2, 2-24-72; Ord. No. 102-85, §
4, 5-30-85)
Sec. 7-2. - Reserved.
Editor's note(s)—Section 7-2, relating to the director, division of treasury,
was repealed by § 13 of Ord. No. 102-85, adopted May 30, 1985. That division
had been abolished by Ord. No. 66-83.
Sec. 7-3. - Director, division of accounting.
The director, division of accounting, also referred to as auditor, shall, under
the supervision of the commissioner of finance, be authorized and empowered and
it shall be his duty, to do and perform all acts and things authorized or
required by general law or ordinances of the urban county government to be
performed by the director, division of accounting. It shall be his duty to
open, and keep in a neat and methodical manner, a complete set of books, under
the direction of the chief administrative officer, wherein he shall state,
among other things, the appropriation for the year for each distinct object and
branch of expenditure, and also the receipts in detail, from each and every
source of revenue, so far as he can ascertain the same. Such books and all
papers, vouchers, contracts, receipts and other things kept by the director,
division of accounting shall be subject to the examination of the mayor and
urban county council members and of the chief administrative officer. He shall
be responsible for processing all requests for cash disbursements, payment of
invoices, and maintaining accounts payable for records. The director, division
of accounting shall also examine periodically the books of the heads of various
departments of the urban county government and shall perform such other duties
as may be required of him by the urban county council or the mayor.
(Ord. No. 102-85, § 5, 5-30-85)
Sec. 7-4. - Director, division of revenue.
The director, division of revenue shall, under the supervision of the
commissioner of finance, be authorized and empowered, and it shall be his duty,
for the collection of all income, revenues and moneys due the urban county
government. It shall be his duty to keep suitable books, in which all his
receipts and disbursements shall be regularly entered, so that the character of
the same shall plainly appear, and in which the accounts of each collector, and
of each fund, shall be separately stated and all accounts of the urban county
government kept correctly and plainly, so that the state of such funds and
accounts may at all times be seen and easily understood. He shall receive all
taxes, licenses, rents and other revenues of the urban county government and
deposit same in the designated depositories, and shall make such disbursements
and perform such other duties as the council or the mayor may order or the
ordinances may require.
(Ord. No. 102-85, § 6, 5-30-85)
Sec. 7-5. - Director, division of central purchasing.
(a)   The director, division of central purchasing and such assistants and
employees subordinate to him as may be necessary for the proper performance of
the work of his office, shall be appointed as provided by law. The director,
division of central purchasing shall be under the supervision of the
commissioner of finance.
(b)   The director, division of central purchasing shall be charged with the
purchase of all supplies, materials and equipment required by the various
departments, boards, commissions, officers and institutions of the urban county
government. Through consultation with the heads of departments and other
administrative officers, boards and commissions, the director, division of
central purchasing shall prepare standard specifications for the supplies,
materials and equipment needed. He shall sell such personal property of the
urban county government as in the opinion of the mayor will not be needed for
further public use. He shall have charge of such storerooms and storehouses of
the urban county government as may be established for the storing of supplies
and materials purchased by the urban county government and not delivered
directly to the various departments, offices, bureaus and commissions. The
director, division of central purchasing shall keep himself informed and
maintain records as to the sources of supply for all classes of purchases,
trends of prices and other matters pertinent to his office. He shall keep a
record of purchases made for the various departments and shall supply the needs
of the various departments on proper requisition.
(c)   No bill for any purchase shall be audited by the director, division of
accounting or paid unless such purchases have been made and approved by either
the chief administrative officer or, in his absence, the commissioner of
finance.
Sec. 7-5.1. - Sworn statement required for bid award.
(1)   A bid shall not be awarded to a bidder until the bidder provides the
division of purchasing with a sworn statement made under penalty of perjury
that:
(a)   The bidder has not knowingly violated any provision of the campaign
finance laws of the Commonwealth within the past five (5) years and that the
award of a contract to the bidder will not violate any provision of the
campaign finance laws of the Commonwealth;
(b)   The bidder will pay all taxes and fees owed to urban county government at
the time the bid was submitted and will maintain a "current" status in regard
to those taxes and fees;
(c)   The bidder will obtain an urban county government business license, if
applicable; and
(d)   The bidder has not knowingly violated any provision of
Chapter 25 of the urban county government Code of Ordinances.
(2)   "Knowingly" for purposes of this section means, with respect to conduct
or to circumstances described by a statute or ordinance defining an offense,
that a person is aware or should have been aware that his contact is of that
nature or that the circumstance exists.
(Ord. No. 167-95, § 1, 7-13-95)
Sec. 7-6. - Alternative approval process for price contracts.
(a)   For purchases utilizing either: price contracts, or fixed price bids or
sole source procurements that only require the Urban County Government to enter
into a unilateral contract or issue a purchase order, and for which the funds
have been budgeted, the administration may place a summary of the acceptance,
approval, and establishment of each such procurement on the Mayor's Report for
Council approval in lieu of a resolution for each procurement.
(b)   At a minimum, the following information must be provided for each
procurement: the name of the department or division for which the procurement
is being made, a description of the goods or services being procured, and the
name(s) of the successful bidder(s).
